instruction: I'm looking for a beach resort for my next vacation. Can you recommend some popular ones?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm going to the mall to do some window shopping. What's the point of window shopping if I'm not going to buy anything?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm looking for pet-friendly activities to do with my family. We have a dog.
reply: Search "dog friendly pubs" and the town name: the listings on DogFriendly and PubsGalore are usually accurate and current. In most British towns the old pubs with wooden floors are the safest bet, and a quick phone call settles it.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to keep my home clean and germ-free. What's the best way to sanitize my kitchen counters?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my social media app. It keeps crashing. Do I need to update it?
reply: Force the app closed and open it again first, then update it in the App Store or Play Store: an app that is behind the phone's software is the usual cause. If it still will not open, restart the phone, then check the phone has storage free (an almost-full phone cannot run apps), and as a last step delete the app and reinstall it, which keeps your account but loses anything saved only on the phone.

instruction: It's raining outside, what should I wear?
reply: A waterproof with a hood is the one thing that decides the day, with a thin layer underneath rather than a thick coat, because rain gear is warm once you move. Wear shoes that keep water out - leather or a waterproof boot rather than canvas, which soaks and stays wet - and take a second pair of socks.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in school. Can you tell me about some shapes I see in everyday objects?
reply: A sphere is the solid round shape where every point on the surface is the same distance from the centre, like a ball or a marble. Its volume is 4/3 times pi times the radius cubed, and its surface area is 4 times pi times the radius squared.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I'm not sure which one to choose. I want something with good quality, but I don't want to spend too much money.
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation in animals. What is camouflage?
reply: They stretch or squeeze layers of pigment cells in the skin. It is mostly mood and temperature rather than camouflage: a calm chameleon is often green, and a cross one goes bright or dark.

instruction: I'm trying to balance my team sports with individual fitness. Do you have any tips?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for a new music streaming platform. What are some popular options?
reply: Worth it if you work or stream at home, more than one person uses the connection, or you game: a phone hotspot will do for one light user, but its data cap and the delay on a video call show up fast. 5g home broadband sits between the two - no line and no engineer, but check the coverage at your postcode and how it holds up at 8pm before you take a two-year deal.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's a good movie soundtrack?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm planning a party for my sister's graduation. What are some common ways to recognize achievements at family celebrations?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any bedtime routine tips?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat lunch. What types of restaurants do you recommend?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up early in the morning. Do you have any tips?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: What is the largest desert in the world?
reply: Dessert is the sweet course, and it has two s's because you want more of it. Desert, one s, is sand or the verb to abandon; the stress moves too - DESSert, deSERT.

instruction: I'm looking for a good video conferencing platform for work. What are some popular options?
reply: Match the limit to the age: under two, video calls and the odd photo only; two to five, an hour of good programmes a day; older children, a set amount agreed in advance. Watch it with them when you can, keep screens away from meals and the hour before bed, and have one screen-free part of each day so it isn't a fight every time.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I was wondering if you had any suggestions.
reply: Make the first session tiny and today: open the topic list, pick the one you know least, and test yourself on it for ten minutes, because starting is the part that is failing rather than the studying. Then put three short sessions in the week you actually have, each ending with a self-test instead of a reread, and give each one a stopping time so it cannot drift to midnight.

instruction: I'm redecorating my living room and I'm looking for some inspiration. Do you have any home styling techniques you can suggest?
reply: Pick the thing you cannot change - the floor, the tiles, the worktop, the sofa - and take the wall colour out of it in a paler version of itself. Then add one deeper tone from the same family for a rug or cushions and a wood or a metal to warm it: three colours, one of them a near-neutral.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. What's the importance of REM sleep?
reply: Sleeping on your side, cutting out alcohol in the evening and losing a little weight fix it for most people who snore, and a blocked nose is worth treating with a decongestant or a steroid spray from the chemist for a couple of weeks to see. A pillow that keeps you off your back, or a tennis ball sewn into the back of a top, does the side-sleeping job.

instruction: I'm feeling really thirsty and my mouth is dry. Is that a sign of dehydration?
reply: Thirst means your body is slightly short of water and your blood has become a little more concentrated; your brain responds by making you want a drink and your kidneys concentrate your urine. If you are always thirsty and passing a lot of urine, get it checked, because that can be diabetes.

instruction: What's a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm planning a family game night. Do you have any suggestions for games?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay active and healthy. What's a good team sport to try?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat. What kinds of restaurants are there?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I love going shopping, especially window shopping. What's the point of window displays?
reply: It is paint gluing the sash to the frame: run a sharp knife, held flat, round the join between the frame and the opening sash to cut the paint film, then work a thin scraper or a wide chisel gently into the gap and ease the window open rather than forcing the handle. Once it is open, sand the paint off the meeting faces and rub a candle or silicone spray along them.

instruction: I'm looking for a new play to watch. What are some popular plays right now?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in school. What is energy conversion?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm learning about minerals in school, and I was wondering what quartz is.
reply: A mineral is a natural solid with a definite chemical make-up and a crystal structure, formed in the earth without anything living making it: quartz, calcite and iron ore are minerals. A rock is usually a mixture of minerals.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes. Do you know any good brands?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay active during the summer. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Take a warm mid layer and a waterproof shell, plus long sleeves rather than vests - even in June the evenings drop to about 8C. Add a hat and gloves if you are going high or out on the water, and midge repellent for anywhere damp and windless in high summer.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried she's not getting enough exercise. How often should I play with her?
reply: Two or three play sessions a day of ten to fifteen minutes each, with a wand toy that moves like a bird or a mouse, and finish each one with a small meal so the hunt ends in a catch. That is plenty for an indoor cat; a laser pointer should always end on something she can actually pounce on, or it leaves her wound up.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to cook my favorite beef stew. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Make the vegetarian dish the main for the whole table and put the meat on the side as an extra: a mushroom and lentil lasagne, a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. Nobody gets a plate of sides, and you cook one dinner.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cooking technique to try. What's braising?
reply: Use 20% fat beef mince, shape loose patties about 2cm thick and press a dent in the middle with your thumb so they stay flat as they cook. Over a high heat, give them 3 minutes a side for medium and rest them 2 minutes before they go in the bun.

instruction: I'm trying to learn more about my family history, especially my grandparents. Can you help me get started?
reply: Sort first, digitise second, and keep the paper: tip the lot onto a table and pull out the faces you cannot lose - the ones people will want in fifty years - then photograph each of those on a phone against a plain background, or use a flatbed scanner for the important ones. Store the prints in an acid-free box somewhere dry and dark rather than a hot loft, write the names and dates on the back of the keepers in pencil, and give the duplicates to the cousins who are in them.

instruction: I'm learning about animals in school. What do polar bears live in?
reply: Penguins live in the southern half of the world: Antarctica, and the coasts of South America, Africa, Australia and New Zealand. There are none at the North Pole; the birds there are puffins, which are not penguins.

instruction: I'm looking for a new multiplayer game to play with my friends. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Codenames* is the one to bring to a group: two teams, one word grid, and it works from four players up. *Wavelength* and *Just One* are the same idea for people who do not like arguing, and for a big party *Werewolf* or *Mafia* needs nothing but a deck of cards.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to buy some souvenirs. What are some popular things to bring back?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm looking for a new basketball. What are some popular brands?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my research paper. Can you suggest some academic journals?
reply: Apply on UCAS: one form, up to five courses, the personal statement and a reference, with 15 October for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine and veterinary science and mid-January for everything else. The statement is the part people worry about, and the rule is to start with the subject, not your childhood: what you have read, built or done that made you want it, then what you want to learn next.

instruction: I want to make a dessert, but I'm not a good cook. Do you have any easy recipes?
reply: Bake something that is low in sugar by nature rather than swapping in sweeteners: an almond and olive oil cake, a carrot cake made with less sugar and more spice, or berries with cream and a little dark chocolate. Keep the portion small and have it after a meal rather than on its own, and put the fruit and the cream on the plate so the cake slice can be thinner.

instruction: I'm interested in animal communication. Do animals talk to each other?
reply: Small mammals: a tawny owl lives on mice, voles and shrews, with the odd small bird, frog or beetle, and a barn owl is almost all voles. It swallows the prey whole and coughs up the fur and bones as a pellet, which is what you find under a roost.

instruction: I'm looking for a new phone case for my iPhone. What types of cases are available?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I was wondering, how do we measure rain?
reply: The sun evaporates water, it rises and cools into cloud droplets, and the droplets bump together until they're heavy enough to fall. Rain is just that water coming back down, usually after a cloud has grown thick and tall.

instruction: I'm worried about the heavy rain forecasted for this weekend. Are there any ways to prevent flooding in my neighborhood?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm going to be in New York for a week and I need a car. What are my options for car rentals?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm trying to find my personal style. Where do I start?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I want to save money. What's a good way to start?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm interested in plants. What kind of plants grow in the desert?
reply: For a sunny border: lavender, salvia, verbena, sedum, rudbeckia, cosmos and a grass or two give colour from June to October and take the heat. Plant in spring or early autumn and water them well through their first summer, because that is what makes them drought-proof later; after that, a mulch in spring is most of the work.

instruction: I'm going to Japan soon and I want to know more about traditional Japanese clothing.
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed at work and I'm looking for some ways to relax during my breaks. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Something slow and ordinary an hour or two before, with water: porridge, toast and egg, or cereal and a banana. A sugary breakfast spikes and drops you by the second hour, which is exactly when the paper gets hard, so keep the sweet thing for the break.

instruction: What is a square?
reply: A square number is what you get when a whole number is multiplied by itself: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on, because 4 × 4 = 16. It is called square because that many dots make a square grid, and it is always a whole number.

instruction: I'm feeling unwell and I'm not sure if I should go to the doctor.
reply: Going often is worth a check rather than a guess: drink water through the day and cut tea, coffee and alcohol for a week to see if it settles. If it carries on, or you are thirsty all the time and passing a lot, see a GP for a blood sugar and urine test, and go the same day if there is blood, a fever or a pain in your back or side.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some whole foods I should include in my diet?
reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm thinking about joining a basketball team. What do I need to do to get started?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for some relaxation techniques. I've heard of Tai chi, what is it?
reply: CBT stands for cognitive behavioural therapy: a short talking treatment that works on the loop between what you think, what you do and how you feel, usually six to twenty weekly sessions with something to try between them. It is what the NHS offers first for anxiety and low mood, and in England you can refer yourself to it without seeing a GP.

instruction: I have two siblings and I want to spend more quality time with them. What are some fun bonding activities we can do together?
reply: Do one thing you could not do with them in the house and one thing that is only rest, and put the fun one first, because the tidying can wait until Sunday evening. The first night can feel strange and quiet, and that is normal rather than a sign anything is wrong.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about musical instruments. What's a popular wind instrument?
reply: A diamond or a delta, about 1.2 to 1.5 metres across, is the usual first kite: it launches easily, flies in light wind and costs about fifteen to twenty-five pounds. Look for one with a long tail (it steadies the flight for a child) and a line of at least 30 metres on a winder.

instruction: I'm looking for some new casual work clothes. What are some popular styles right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gaming platform. What's the difference between PlayStation and Xbox?
reply: A console is cheaper and simpler: it plays everything at good quality for years, no upgrades, and you can sell it on. A gaming PC costs more up front but gets cheaper games, higher settings and mods, and doubles as a work machine - so pick the console for a shared living room and the PC if you already sit at a desk with a monitor.

instruction: I'm learning about ecosystems in school. What is an ecosystem?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping. How can I stay safe?
reply: Use a virtual card: most banking apps make a one-off card number in a few taps, so the shop never holds the real details, and set a low limit on it. Where that is not offered, one card kept for online only, notifications on for every payment, and the real one frozen in the app between uses - most let you unfreeze it in seconds.

instruction: I'm trying to build a capsule wardrobe, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I've been noticing some water damage on my ceiling, and I'm not sure if I should fix it myself or call a professional.
reply: A brown or yellow patch on a ceiling is water, and the first job is to find where it comes in rather than paint over it. Look at what is above: a bathroom or a radiator pipe means a leak at the sealant, the trap or the joint, and an outside wall or the roof means it only grows after rain, so note whether it does.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some popular sleep aids?
reply: Sleeping on your side, cutting out alcohol in the evening and losing a little weight fix it for most people who snore, and a blocked nose is worth treating with a decongestant or a steroid spray from the chemist for a couple of weeks to see. A pillow that keeps you off your back, or a tennis ball sewn into the back of a top, does the side-sleeping job.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Greek cuisine. What's a popular Greek dish?
reply: Natural is milk and cultures and nothing else, and it is what to cook with. Greek is the same yoghurt strained of its whey, so it is thicker and higher in protein; Greek-style is thickened with milk powder and is cheaper and sweeter.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping this weekend. Can you help me with my grocery list?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy breakfast idea. What's a good option?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm trying to stay healthy. What's the best way to prevent the spread of germs?
reply: Stand them in a rack, spaced so the air gets round, and let them air-dry: a tea towel mostly moves the water about. If you do use one, wash your hands first and change the towel daily, because a damp cloth that sits out is where the germs come from.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New Zealand and I'm looking for some adventure activities to do.
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting hobbies?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the mountains and I want to capture some beautiful landscapes. What's the best time of day to take photos?
reply: Get daylight as soon as you can after landing, eat at local meal times, and keep caffeine to the local morning. Sleeping on arrival makes it worse; a short 20-minute nap before 3pm is the most you want.

instruction: I want to bake some bread. What ingredients do I need?
reply: Flour, water, salt and yeast. The yeast gives off gas as it feeds on the flour, and the gluten in the flour - stretchy because it is wheat - traps it as bubbles, which is what makes the loaf rise; the oven then sets the structure and browns the crust.

instruction: I'm learning about fossils in school. How are they formed?
reply: A fossil forms when a dead animal or plant is buried quickly and its hard parts are slowly replaced by minerals from the surrounding rock over thousands of years. Most living things rot away entirely, which is why fossils are rare.

instruction: I'm going shopping this weekend and I'm looking for some discounts. Do you know of any sales happening?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure what type of work I want to do. Can you tell me some common job categories?
reply: Lead with what you have done, not with job titles: school or college, volunteering, a paper round, a team you played in, a club you ran. Then a two-line profile at the top saying what you want and what you are good at with people, numbers or tools.

instruction: I'm looking for information about my favorite TV show. What's the process of making a TV series?
reply: *Serial* series one is where to start: one murder, a year of reporting, and the reason everyone else started making them. Then *Casefile* (calm, one case an episode), *Criminal* (short, strange cases, less grim) or *The Teacher's Pet* if you want one long story done properly.

instruction: I'm looking for a new multiplayer game to play. What's a popular one?
reply: *Codenames* is the one to bring to a group: two teams, one word grid, and it works from four players up. *Wavelength* and *Just One* are the same idea for people who do not like arguing, and for a big party *Werewolf* or *Mafia* needs nothing but a deck of cards.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding some of the books I'm reading for school. Do you have any tips on how to improve my comprehension?
reply: Testing yourself is what makes things stick; rereading notes mostly feels productive without being so. Turn each topic into five questions and answer them with the book shut, then check, and redo the ones you got wrong tomorrow and again in a week.

instruction: I want to improve my cardiovascular health. What are some good exercises for that?
reply: Walking counts, and brisk walking for 30 minutes most days does most of what a gentle gym session would for your heart and mood. Add two short strength sessions a week for muscle and bone, and pick up the pace until you are slightly out of breath.

instruction: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's birthday. I have a budget of $50.
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to save money on my daily commute to work. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm learning about space and gravity. What is gravity in space?
reply: There is gravity in space: astronauts on the space station float because they and the station are falling around the Earth together at the same speed, not because gravity has gone. At that height gravity is still about 90% as strong as it is on the ground.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms. Have you heard of Udemy?
reply: Ask three or four people who have just passed and book a single lesson with the one they liked most - a good instructor is the thing that makes lessons worth the money, and one lesson tells you more than any advert. Look for someone approved by the DVSA (an ADI badge on the windscreen), a quiet manner, and a lesson plan rather than being driven round for two hours.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is groundwater?
reply: Rain soaks into the ground and runs into rivers, and your tap water is drawn from a river, a reservoir or a borehole, then filtered and treated so nothing can grow in it and pumped to the house under pressure. A town near hills is usually fed from a reservoir; anywhere else it comes from a river or from deep underground.

instruction: I'm looking for information about antique furniture. What's the most popular type?
reply: Second-hand furniture is the best value there is, and charity shops and Freecycle are the places to look. Check for woodworm holes, sagging cushions and smoke smell, and measure your door and stairs before you collect anything big.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my dog's behavior, and I'm thinking of working with an animal behaviorist. What does an animal behaviorist do?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm going to my friend's graduation ceremony next week. What's the point of these ceremonies?
reply: The best man looks after the groom and the rings: hold both wedding rings, hand them over at the right moment, keep the groom calm and on time, carry the licence or the paperwork, and look after the gifts and the cards. He organises the stag do and collects for the wedding present from the groom's side, makes sure the groom is dressed, fed and at the ceremony early, and gives the speech after the meal - a short one that thanks the couple on the guests' behalf and embarrasses the groom gently.

instruction: I'm going to a concert next weekend and I want to buy a t-shirt. What's the best way to get concert merchandise?
reply: Ask the teacher or the dance school first: for a show they usually name a supplier, sell the costume themselves or keep a rail of spares, and buying the wrong shade of leotard wastes the money. If it is yours to sort, hiring costs less than buying for one night, fancy-dress shops and second-hand marketplaces have plenty a week before, and a plain base layer with two bought accessories reads perfectly well from the audience.

instruction: I'm looking for sports news. What's the latest on the NBA?
reply: Four quarters: 10 minutes each in international (FIBA) games, so 40 minutes of play, and 12 each in the NBA for 48. The clock stops on every whistle, so the whole game takes about two hours.

instruction: I'm trying to establish a daily routine for personal hygiene. What's the most important thing to do every day?
reply: Fifteen minutes a day keeps a house, and the daily fifteen is the same three things: make the bed, wipe the kitchen surfaces and put the dishes away. Then give one room a proper clean on a weekday rota - bathroom on Monday, kitchen on Wednesday, floors on Friday - and leave the weekends for bedding and towels, which is one wash each.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, especially ones that have cultural significance to families.
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: What is toothpaste used for?
reply: Plaque is the soft, sticky film of bacteria that forms on teeth within hours of brushing, feeding on sugar and making the acid that causes decay and sore gums. Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between the teeth once a day shifts it, and once it hardens into tartar only a dentist can scale it off.

instruction: I'm learning about volleyball rotations. What are the main positions in volleyball?
reply: Volleyball starts with the pass: get your feet there early, lock your arms into a platform and let the ball come to you instead of swinging at it - it should go up and to the setter, not forward. A spike is the last touch of three: high approach, arm back, and hit the top half of the ball so it drives down; a dig is the same low platform, absorbing the ball rather than swinging at it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about amusement parks with the best roller coasters. Can you tell me about some popular ones?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I have a question about the human ear. What is the main function of the human ear?
reply: An itchy ear canal is usually dry skin or a touch of eczema, sometimes a little water or wax left behind. Leave cotton buds, keys and hairgrips out of it: they scratch the skin and pack wax against the drum, which is what keeps the itch going.

instruction: I'm looking for a running community to join. Do you know any popular ones?
reply: Parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday at 9am in a local park: register once online, print or screenshot your barcode, and turn up ten minutes early for the first-timers' briefing. Walkers are genuinely welcome and plenty of people walk it, so you will not be last on your own.

instruction: I'm looking for information about team sports leagues. What are some popular team sports leagues in the US?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm planning a family dinner tonight, and my sister is gluten-free. What are some good gluten-free options for main courses?
reply: Gluten is just the protein in wheat, barley and rye, and it is only a problem for the roughly one in a hundred people with coeliac disease, or for a wheat allergy - for everyone else there is nothing to avoid. If bread and pasta leave you bloated, windy or tired, ask the GP for a coeliac blood test before you cut gluten out, because the test only works while you are still eating it.

instruction: I'm thinking about organizing my home. What are the main rooms in a house?
reply: Twenty minutes a room on a timer, top to bottom, floor last: a bin bag for the rubbish and a basket for everything that lives somewhere else, then dust from the ceiling down (corners, the tops of pictures, lamp shades), then wipe the marks, then hoover. For a whole house, do the rooms visitors see in the order they see them - hall, loo, kitchen, sitting room - and shut the doors on the rest.

instruction: What is the Internet of Things?
reply: WiFi does not stand for anything: a branding agency made the word up in 1999 as a play on hi-fi, and the Wireless Ethernet Compatibility Alliance liked it enough to buy it. The thing itself is just a short-range radio link, so there are no letters to expand.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some superfoods I should include in my diet?
reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm worried about the storm that's supposed to hit our area tonight. Will it be severe?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet, but I'm not sure if I'm ready for the long-term commitment.
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm looking for a home workout routine to get started with. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for vaccinations. What are the most common vaccinations for dogs?
reply: Once a year for a dog, and a cat the same: the leptospirosis part of a dog's booster has to be every year, while the distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus parts are often given every three years, so ask the vet which you are due. Kennel cough is the extra one worth having if he goes to a groomer, day care or a boarding kennel.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some over-the-counter sleep aids that I can try?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm a big fan of the TV show "Stranger Things." Do you know when the next season is coming out?
reply: Millie Bobby Brown plays Eleven in Stranger Things (2016-2025).

instruction: I'm feeling tired after lunch. Is napping good for me?
reply: After a big meal, blood flow shifts to the gut and the body clock dips in the early afternoon, so feeling sleepy is normal, especially with a lot of refined carbs or alcohol. A smaller lunch, a short walk and daylight help; see a GP if it happens after every meal with thirst, weight loss or falling asleep mid-conversation.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you know what sleep apnea is?
reply: Sleep apnoea is the airway at the back of the throat closing for ten seconds or more, many times a night, so breathing stops in short bursts and you wake just enough to start again - which is why the snoring breaks off and why eight hours leaves you flat. The signs are loud snoring with silences, a gasp or a choke, a dry mouth and a morning headache, and nodding off in the day; extra weight, a thick neck, alcohol at night and sleeping on your back all make it worse.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines. What is a screw?
reply: A lever is a bar that turns on a pivot, and it lets a small push move a big weight if the pivot sits close to the weight: a crowbar, a wheelbarrow, a see-saw and a bottle opener are all levers.

instruction: I'm feeling overwhelmed with work and struggling to find a balance between work and personal life. Do you have any strategies for prioritizing tasks?
reply: Each morning pick the one task that would make the day a good one, and do it before email. Then batch the small things (messages, approvals) into two set times, and keep a "later" list so you stop holding them in your head; most of the day's stress is unfinished small things, not hard ones.

instruction: What are some popular types of coffee?
reply: Two beans: arabica is the fruity, slightly acidic one in most good coffee, and robusta is stronger, more bitter and has about twice the caffeine, which is why instant and cheap espresso blends use it. Roast runs from light, which keeps the fruit and the acidity, to dark, which tastes of the roast itself.

instruction: I'm trying to study for a test and I was wondering if practice testing is a good way to learn.
reply: Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes. What are some soft textures I should look for?
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.

instruction: I'm thinking about dinner with my family tonight. What are some popular family dinner ideas?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm feeling really tired lately. How much sleep do I need?
reply: An extra hour or two is usually the good call after a short night. Let the sleep happen, then open the curtains and get some daylight.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in my city. What's the main cause of pollution?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to help me stay on track with my workouts. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I'm planning a family gathering this weekend and I want to hear some story ideas to share with my family.
reply: Choose something short you can actually get through: a poem, a psalm or a few lines from a book they loved, read by somebody other than the closest person if you can. Two readings is plenty for a crematorium slot, five to ten minutes of speaking in all.

instruction: I'm thinking of improving my backyard. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Tidy the outline first, because a garden reads as untidy at its edges before its middle: cut the lawn edge right round with a half-moon edger, clear the path, and weed the first foot of border. Then buy three plants and no more - something tall, something scented by the door, and something that flowers for months - in pots if the soil is poor.

instruction: I'm learning to code and I was wondering what programming languages are used for web development.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm looking for information about sustainable fashion trends. What is sustainable fashion?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I want to start working out, but I'm struggling to find motivation. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm cleaning my house and I need a new vacuum cleaner. What types are available?
reply: Check the weight and the cord length before anything else, because the best vacuum is the one you will actually push round the house. A bagged machine holds its suction and suits anyone with allergies; a bagless one is cheaper to run but needs emptying over a bin.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, do you have any family recipes you can share?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm interested in storm chasing. What is storm chasing?
reply: Collisions between ice and water drops in a storm cloud build up electric charge. When the difference gets big enough, the charge leaps through the air as a huge spark: lightning, which heats the air so fast it makes the bang of thunder.

instruction: I'm looking for information about local sports teams in my area. What teams do you have information on?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I've been thinking about walking to work instead of driving. Is walking good for my health?
reply: Walking alone will not do it - what you eat decides most of it - but 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day is a fair target, and the gain is that it burns a little and keeps you from sitting down all day. The quicker half is the plate: a smaller portion of the starch, more protein and vegetables, and no drinks with sugar in.

instruction: What is an even number?
reply: An integer is a whole number - positive, negative or zero - with no fraction or decimal part. So 4, -7 and 0 are integers, while 2.5 and 1/3 are not; the integers are the counting numbers, their negatives, and zero.

instruction: I'm a parent and I'm looking for ideas for a field trip for my child's class.
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow and I'm not sure what to expect.
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to watch. What's popular on Netflix right now?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a pet, what are some good activities to do with them to bond?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm learning about volcanoes in school and I was wondering, what is a volcano?
reply: Lava is molten rock that has come out of a volcano onto the surface; the same stuff underground is magma. It cools into rock, and runny lava flows far while thick lava piles up near the vent.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the beach this weekend, but I'm worried about the weather. Will it be windy?
reply: Yes, with a few things done right. Pick a lifeguarded beach and swim between the flags, go with someone rather than alone, and check the tide and the wind before you get in.

instruction: I'm looking for some new non-fiction books to read. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my work schedule. I have a lot of night shifts this week.
reply: Shift it 15 minutes at a time, not an hour: set the alarm a quarter of an hour earlier every three or four days and go to bed a quarter earlier too, or you just lose sleep. Get daylight on your face within half an hour of waking, and keep the new time at weekends or Monday undoes it.

instruction: I'm looking for some home workout ideas. I don't have any equipment, so I'd like to do bodyweight exercises.
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm getting tired of my daily commute to work. What are some alternatives I could consider?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something I can do at home. I enjoy cooking and trying new recipes.
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm starting to learn about organic chemistry and I was wondering what it's all about.
reply: A chemical reaction is when substances rearrange their atoms to make new ones: bonds break, new bonds form, and the starting materials are used up. Burning, rusting, baking and digestion are all reactions, and they usually give out or take in heat.

instruction: I'm planning to start a garden in my backyard, but I'm not sure if my soil is ready. What's the best way to prepare it?
reply: Use a peat-free multi-purpose with a good third of perlite or grit stirred through for drainage, or a ready-made houseplant mix, which is the same thing in one bag. Garden soil in a pot sets like concrete and brings in pests, so leave it outside.

instruction: I want to make a simple one-pot dish for dinner. What are some easy options?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting and I want to start a gym routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Learn five movements and ignore everything else for a month: squat, hinge (deadlift), push, pull and carry. Two or three sessions a week, three sets of 8–12, adding a little weight each time.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some fun things to do with them?
reply: Small things they can use lying in bed: a long phone cable and a charged power bank, earphones, a puzzle book or a magazine, a decent lip balm, a light blanket, or a printed photo of the family to put on the locker. Skip flowers on most wards and skip food unless you know the diet.

instruction: I'm looking for a new toy for my cat. What are some popular pet toys?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What's the optimal room temperature for a good night's sleep?
reply: A bedroom around 16 to 18C suits most people for sleep: cool enough that you need a duvet, not so cold you wake up. Cracking a window for ten minutes before bed, a lighter duvet in summer and a hot water bottle rather than a hot room all help, and a warm bath an hour before bed sends you to sleep faster than a warm bedroom does.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming festivals. Can you tell me about Diwali?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get more vitamin D. What are some natural sources of it?
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm not sure if I'm sleeping enough. How much sleep do adults need?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier, but I'm not sure how to read food labels.
reply: Ultra-processed food is the industrial end of the scale: things made mostly from extracts and additives - emulsifiers, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners - that you would not cook with at home, like fizzy drinks, crisps, sausages, ready meals and most breakfast cereal. The evidence is that people eat more of it and put on weight, but the class is broad enough that hummus and wholemeal bread land in it, so judge by the ingredient list rather than the label.

instruction: I'm thinking of setting up a smart home system. What's the main device that controls everything?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm planning a dinner party and I have guests with dietary restrictions. Do you have any suggestions for gluten-free meals?
reply: Gluten is just the protein in wheat, barley and rye, and it is only a problem for the roughly one in a hundred people with coeliac disease, or for a wheat allergy - for everyone else there is nothing to avoid. If bread and pasta leave you bloated, windy or tired, ask the GP for a coeliac blood test before you cut gluten out, because the test only works while you are still eating it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new smart thermostat for my home. What are some popular brands?

Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm thinking of replacing my air conditioner. What's the difference between a window unit and a central air system?
reply: A fan costs a penny or two an hour; a portable air conditioner is more like 30 to 50p, and a fitted one more again. A fan only cools you, not the room, so put it in front of an open window at night with another window open across the room.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something exciting. What sports do you recommend?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to engage my students in the classroom. Have you heard of game-based learning?
reply: Keep instructions under twenty seconds, show it once, then let them try it in a game — children learn by playing, not by queueing to take turns. Give every child a job or a ball, praise the one who does the thing you asked, and change the game every ten minutes.

instruction: I'm looking for a new watch. What are some popular brands?
reply: A watch battery is a coin cell, usually a CR2016, CR2025 or CR2032 printed inside the back, and the number matters: a jeweller will fit the right one for a few pounds, and many watch shops do it while you wait. Doing it yourself needs a case-back tool, and a watch with a screw-down back or any water resistance is worth leaving to them, because the seal has to go back clean or it will fog up.

instruction: I'm looking for information about community theater in my area. Do you know how I can find local theater groups?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm feeling stuck in the office, is it healthy to spend a lot of time indoors?
reply: Nobody can tell you before you go: a walk-in centre sees people in the order they need seeing rather than the order they arrived, so a queue of two hours can move in twenty minutes when something urgent comes in, and a quiet room can still mean a long wait. Ring the centre or look at its own site on the day for the wait it is running, and go early rather than late in the evening.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Europe and I'm not sure about travel insurance. Do I really need it?
reply: Take the free GHIC card for state healthcare in the EU and pair it with proper travel insurance: the card covers treatment, not getting you home. Buy insurance when you book so cancellation is included.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip this weekend. What are some traffic safety tips I should keep in mind?
reply: Get left and off the carriageway if you still can, then hazards on. Everyone out of the doors on the left, behind the barrier, and well back from the car: never stand between it and the traffic, and never change a wheel on a motorway.

instruction: I'm looking for information about designer collaborations. Can you tell me about the latest one between Louis Vuitton and Nike?
reply: Bluetooth is a short-range radio link, about ten metres, that your phone and the other device use to talk directly without a network or a router. They hop channels 1,600 times a second so they do not collide with wifi, and pairing is simply the two agreeing a key once so they recognise each other afterwards.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of a butterfly. What's the first stage?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm looking for some new casual wear ideas. What's popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some ways I can stay close to them?
reply: Do the inviting yourself, and make it the same thing each week - a walk on Tuesday, a coffee on Saturday - because a standing date is easy to say yes to and does not need them to suggest anything. Ask specifically and name the day, ring rather than text, and keep asking after a no, since the first answer from someone lonely is often no.

reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm having trouble getting my kids to bed on time. Do you have any bedtime routine tips?
reply: Make bedtime the same five steps in the same order every night - bath, milk, teeth, two books, lights out - and put them down at the same minute, awake. When they get up, walk them back with as few words as possible, as many times as it takes; the calm repetition is what does the work, and it usually sorts itself out in about a week.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan and I want to take some amazing photos. What are some good composition techniques for travel photography?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm trying to understand more about social media influencers. What's the main goal of an influencer?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account. Private means new people have to ask to follow you, but it does not hide anything from the people already following, so check that list too.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school and I was wondering, what's a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear during the summer. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.

instruction: What's the weather like in summer?
reply: Summer is hotter because the Sun is higher in the sky and stays up longer, so the same patch of ground gets more direct sunlight and more hours of it. The Earth is actually farthest from the Sun in July, which is why distance is not the explanation.

instruction: I'm looking for some new ideas for family meals. What are some popular family dinner traditions?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What is the Olympic legacy?
reply: Pick one theme for the year rather than ten goals, then turn it into three actions with dates: "run 5k by June - book a race in January, run twice a week" does more than "get fit". Make each one small enough to start in ten minutes on a bad day, put the first step in the diary this week, and look at the list once a month rather than every day.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what to pack.
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I need to measure some ingredients for a recipe. What's the difference between a cup and a pint?
reply: A spoonful means a level tablespoon, 15ml unless the recipe says heaped; a cupful is 250ml, filled level rather than heaped. Go by the recipe where it gives a weight.

instruction: I'm looking for a new social media platform to join. What's popular right now?
reply: The paid tiers are small money: iCloud+ gives 50GB for about £1 a month and 200GB for about £3, Google One 100GB for roughly £1.60 and 200GB for about £2.50, and Dropbox starts near £10 for 2TB. A photo is about 3MB, so 200GB holds well over 50,000 of them, and most people with a full phone need that one rather than the largest.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated, but I'm not sure how much water I should be drinking.
reply: Six to eight glasses a day, about 1.5 to 2 litres, is plenty, and more in heat or after exercise; tea, coffee, milk, squash and food all count towards it, and pale straw-coloured urine is the check that you are about right. If you forget, keep a filled bottle where you sit and drink a glass with every meal.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. Why are plants important?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what kind of luggage to get. What are my options?
reply: Start with the airline, because cabin sizes differ: a 55x40x20cm case fits most paid cabin allowances, while the free underseat bag is around 40x20x25cm, and a bag outside the airline's own limit is the one thing that gets charged at the gate. Four wheels and a hard polycarbonate shell survive the hold better, soft bags give and squash into a car; either way check the empty weight against a 23kg allowance and buy from a brand that covers wheels and handles for years rather than months.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of custards?
reply: Homemade custard keeps 2 days in the fridge, in a jug with a lid or a sheet of cling film pressed onto the surface so no skin forms. Reheat it gently and stir rather than boiling it, and bin any that has stood on the table through dinner.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about galaxies. What is a galaxy?
reply: A galaxy is a huge group of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity; galaxies form as clouds of gas and dark matter pull together. Our Milky Way holds 100 to 400 billion stars and is about 100,000 light years across, and there are billions of galaxies beyond it, most with a supermassive black hole at the centre.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping because I work night shifts. What's a good bedtime routine for someone like me?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm planning to do some gardening this weekend. What are the best tools to use for pruning and trimming?
reply: A gardener is usually £20 to £35 an hour, and a fortnightly cut of a small lawn is £30 to £50 a visit. One-off clearances, hedges and anything with a skip are priced by the job instead.

instruction: I'm looking for a new place to eat. What types of restaurants are there?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm interested in boxing. What are some popular boxing styles?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm planning a family reunion and I want to know more about common family traditions.
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family traditions. What are some common family traditions?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm having trouble with time management at work. Do you have any tips?
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: I had a weird dream last night. Can you help me understand what it means?
reply: Nightmares usually follow stress, late food, alcohol or a heavy film before bed, so start there. If the same one keeps coming back, write it down in the day and rehearse a different ending a few times: that is the technique that works.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my home office and get rid of all the paper clutter. Do you have any tips for managing paperwork?
reply: Start with what is on the floor: pick it all up into one basket, take the cups and plates out to the kitchen and bin the rubbish, because clothes, cups and paper are most of a mess and that alone makes a room look tidy. Then wipe the one surface you use most - the worktop, the table or the bedside - and give the rest one room a day rather than all of it in a panic.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smart speaker for my home. What's the difference between Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm going on a trip tomorrow and I'm not sure what to pack in my carry-on.
reply: Lay everything out and take half the clothes and twice the money: three tops, two bottoms, one warm layer and shoes you can walk in covers a week. Roll clothes, keep a change in your hand luggage, and buy anything you forget when you arrive.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to track my workouts. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something interesting to collect. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape and boost my endurance. What's a good way to start?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm planning to set up my home office. What are the basic things I need to have in a home office?
reply: Two pens, a pencil, a spare, an eraser, and your photo ID plus the letter with the room and the time on it. A clear bottle of water if the rules allow one, and nothing else in your pockets - a phone switched off still counts as being in the room, so leave it at home.

instruction: I'm having trouble keeping up with my schoolwork and homework. Do you have any tips for managing my time?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way.
