If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm looking for a core workout routine to improve my overall fitness. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm trying to study more effectively. What's spaced repetition?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a list. Can you help me organize it?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for some new streetwear fashion ideas. What's currently trending?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I was wondering about magnets. What are the poles of a magnet?
reply: A magnet has a magnetic field, and it pulls on materials whose electrons can line up with that field, like iron, nickel and cobalt. Cut a magnet in half and you get two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole.

instruction: I'm having trouble staying focused on my homework. Do you have any tips?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm looking for some deals on electronics. Do you know of any online sales happening now?
reply: Check two things before you sell: the trade-in price from the network or the maker, and what the same model with the same storage sells for on a resale site - the private sale is often 20 to 30% more. Say the battery health and any marks honestly, sign out of your accounts and factory reset it in front of the buyer.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of flats. What are some popular styles?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm a student and I'm looking for some discounts on laptops. Do you know of any sales going on?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for a new vet for my cat, do you have any tips on how to find a good one?
reply: Book boarding early, ask your vet for a recommendation, and visit before you book: clean, calm and willing to show you the runs tells you more than any website. A pet sitter at home suits cats far better than a cattery.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up in the morning. Do you know any techniques to help me wake up more gently?
reply: Go in quietly, keep the light off, say the same short thing and walk them back, so waking up gains nothing. Then look at the day: a nap that runs past three, a bedtime too early or too late, a room too warm, or a drink of milk that has become the reason to wake.

instruction: I'm taking a first aid class and I'm not sure how to do CPR. Can you tell me the steps?
reply: A heart attack is a blocked blood supply to the heart muscle - the person is usually awake, with chest pain, and needs an ambulance fast. A cardiac arrest is the heart stopping altogether: unresponsive and not breathing normally, needing CPR and a defibrillator at once - call 999 first.

instruction: I'm looking for information about maps. What's the difference between a map and a globe?
reply: In Google Maps tap your picture > Offline maps > Select your own map, frame the area you need and download it; it stays usable for about a year and works with the phone in airplane mode. On an iPhone, Apple Maps keeps recent routes offline and a dedicated app such as Organic Maps covers the same ground for free.

instruction: I'm on-call this weekend. What does that mean exactly?
reply: Answer once, in advance, rather than each time it happens: "I'm off tomorrow. I'll pick up anything non-urgent on Thursday morning, and if something cannot wait, call me on this number." Then do not answer the ordinary messages - a reply on a day off teaches people that the day off is available.

instruction: I'm interested in sports. What are some popular sports in the world?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm learning about buoyancy in school and I was wondering, what is density?
reply: Buoyancy is the upward push a liquid or gas gives anything in it, equal to the weight of the fluid it pushes aside. A steel ship floats because the air inside makes it push aside more water than the ship itself weighs, while a solid lump of steel cannot.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how often I should trim his nails.
reply: Every six to eight weeks is plenty for most dogs, and less for a short coat: use a dog shampoo rather than yours, because a dog's skin sits at a different pH. Wet him right down to the skin, lather, then rinse for twice as long as feels necessary - leftover shampoo is what causes the scratching afterwards.

instruction: I'm learning about earth and soil formation in school, can you tell me how soil is formed?
reply: Soil is crushed rock mixed with rotted plant and animal matter, plus air, water and a vast number of microbes. The rotted part, humus, is what holds water and feeds plants, and it takes hundreds of years to build up an inch of it.

instruction: I'm going for a walk outside, but it looks like it might rain. Should I bring an umbrella?
reply: That is a question about the hours you will actually be out, not about the day: under about 10 degrees, yes, and a proper coat with a jumper under it if you will be standing about; between 10 and 18 a jumper and something windproof is enough, and over 18 you carry the coat rather than wear it. Rain decides it more often than cold does, so a waterproof beats a warmer one that lets water through, and the bits that feel it first are the neck, ears, hands and feet.

instruction: I'm concerned about pollution in my city. What's the main cause of noise pollution?
reply: If the noise is coming from outside your room, earplugs and a heavy curtain take the edge off, and a fan or white noise can mask it. If it is a neighbour and it happens often, your council's noise team can act on it; a short log of the times is what they ask for.

instruction: I have a brother and we always fight. What can I do?
reply: Name it once without defending yourself - "it can't have felt fair, watching me get that" - and then ask what it was like from where they stood, which is the only thing that shifts it. Arguing the facts never does: a jealous brother is not short of facts, he is short of a hearing.

instruction: I'm feeling tired after lunch. Is napping good for productivity?
reply: After a big meal, blood flow shifts to the gut and the body clock dips in the early afternoon, so feeling sleepy is normal, especially with a lot of refined carbs or alcohol. A smaller lunch, a short walk and daylight help; see a GP if it happens after every meal with thirst, weight loss or falling asleep mid-conversation.

instruction: I'm having trouble reading my school books. Do you have any tips?
reply: Testing yourself is what makes things stick; rereading notes mostly feels productive without being so. Turn each topic into five questions and answer them with the book shut, then check, and redo the ones you got wrong tomorrow and again in a week.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. What affects sleep quality?
reply: Long sleeps now and then are just a debt being paid, especially after a run of short nights. Needing nine or ten hours most nights and still waking flat is worth a GP visit: an underactive thyroid, low iron, low vitamin D, depression and sleep apnoea all show up that way, and each is easy to test for.

instruction: I'm going to a networking event for my industry, and I'm not sure what to expect. What's the main goal of networking events?
reply: It is what people say to someone before a show or a match: it means good luck, because wishing it out loud is thought to jinx it. What are you going on for?

instruction: I'm looking for a new home entertainment system. What are my options?
reply: Take one at a time, a month at a time, and cancel when the series ends: almost every service sells monthly with no contract, so a year of switching costs far less than a year of all of them. Two are worth keeping at once at most - one for the family boxsets and one for what you watch live, football or the soaps.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the weather forecast. Is a storm coming to my area?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the best time for a nap?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm learning about renewable and non-renewable resources in school. What's the difference between the two?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm graduating from high school soon. What are some common graduation traditions?
reply: Buy to the list the school sends, not to the supermarket display, and buy two of the things that get worn out: two jumpers with the badge, two or three polo shirts, two pairs of trousers or skirts, a PE kit in the school colours and plimsolls for indoors. A child starting in reception also needs a spare set of clothes in a bag for the first weeks and wellies if they play outside.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is the water cycle?
reply: Water evaporates from the sea and land, rises and cools into clouds, falls as rain or snow, and runs back to the sea: the same water goes round and round. Sunlight drives it and gravity brings it back down.

instruction: I'm trying to get to downtown from my neighborhood. What local bus route should I take?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm looking for different types of coffee. What are some popular varieties?
reply: Two beans: arabica is the fruity, slightly acidic one in most good coffee, and robusta is stronger, more bitter and has about twice the caffeine, which is why instant and cheap espresso blends use it. Roast runs from light, which keeps the fruit and the acidity, to dark, which tastes of the roast itself.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we all live together. What are some ways we can share household responsibilities?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources to learn about history. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Start with *The Rest Is History* (two funny historians), *Desert Island Discs* for people talking about their lives, or *Casefile* if you want a true crime story told straight. Tell me what you usually listen to and I'll aim closer.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to track my workouts. What are some popular options?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I love sunny days, they make me happy. Does sunshine really affect our mood?
reply: Affect is the verb and effect is the noun: the weather affects my mood, and the weather has an effect on my mood. A useful memory: 'cause and effect' is always the noun.

instruction: I'm going to meet my in-laws for the first time this weekend. Do you have any advice?
reply: Do the inviting yourself, and make it the same thing each week - a walk on Tuesday, a coffee on Saturday - because a standing date is easy to say yes to and does not need them to suggest anything. Ask specifically and name the day, ring rather than text, and keep asking after a no, since the first answer from someone lonely is often no.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the planets in our solar system. What's the biggest planet?
reply: Jupiter is the biggest planet: about 143,000 km across, or 11 Earths side by side, and more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

instruction: I'm trying to create a daily bathing routine. What's the recommended frequency for showering?
reply: Two or three times a week is plenty for most adults, with a wash of the face, hands, feet, under the arms and the groin every day; the rest of the skin can wait. Five to ten minutes and lukewarm is enough for a whole shower, and long hot ones strip the oils out of dry skin, so moisturise while it is still damp.

instruction: I'm planning a vacation to Europe and I'm looking for suggestions on historical landmarks to visit.
reply: Christopher Columbus reached the Caribbean in 1492, sailing for Spain, and thought he had found a route to Asia. He never set foot in North America itself; the Vikings had reached Newfoundland about 500 years earlier.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you know anything about sleep disorders?
reply: Fix the wake-up time first: the same hour every day, including after a bad night, and the rest tends to follow within a fortnight. Then the three that do most of the work - daylight and a walk in the first hour, no caffeine after lunch, and a screen-free half hour before bed - and only get into bed when you are sleepy rather than tired.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my learning skills. What's mind mapping?
reply: Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm looking for advice on how to recover after a run.
reply: Nearly all running injuries come from doing more, sooner than the body can repair: add no more than about 10 per cent to your weekly distance, keep every second run easy, and take a rest day after a long one. Two short strength sessions a week - calf raises, squats, a single-leg balance - and shoes that are not worn through do the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to modernize my family's classic recipes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I was wondering what the most popular form of communication is today.
reply: Writing began around 3200 BC in Mesopotamia, as marks for accounting: quantities of grain and sheep. Independent systems appeared later in Egypt, China and Mesoamerica.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's popular on music streaming platforms right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do weighted blankets really help?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to share my family recipes online. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Three that work with children, easiest first: flapjack (no oven hands, just stirring and a flat tin), fairy cakes (they can fill the cases and ice them once cool) and shortbread (three ingredients, and cutting shapes is the fun part). Give the little ones the measuring and the stirring and keep the oven and the hob to yourself, and expect it to take twice as long as it would alone.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting some smart home devices to help me save energy. What's a good place to start?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a dog, and I want to know if they need a lot of exercise.
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm looking for new sports shoes. What are some popular brands?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I want to take some great photos. What camera equipment should I bring?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm learning about colors in art. What are primary colors?
reply: Pot a red (1 point), then a colour (2 to 7), and put the colour back on its spot; carry on that way until the reds are gone, then take the colours in order. The maximum break is 147: fifteen reds with fifteen blacks, then all the colours.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any tips on how to establish a sleep routine?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I love colors in nature. What's the most common color in flowers?
reply: Blue is scattered much more strongly than green, so the green that is scattered arrives mixed with far more blue and the sky reads as pale blue. Violet is scattered even more, but there is less of it in sunlight and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so it never dominates.

instruction: I'm learning about American history in school and I was wondering when the United States declared its independence.
reply: The American colonies declared independence from Britain on 4 July 1776, and won it after fighting until 1783. The Declaration's argument, that governments rule by the consent of the governed, is why the date still matters.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what's the best camera type for a beginner.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm thinking of remodeling my kitchen. What are some popular materials for countertops?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm trying to calculate the cost of items at the store. If a shirt costs $15 and I have a 10% discount coupon, how much will I pay?
reply: To find a percentage of something, divide the amount by 100 and multiply by the percentage: 15% of 80 is 80 ÷ 100 × 15 = 12. To turn a fraction into a percentage, divide the top by the bottom and multiply by 100.

instruction: My computer is running slow. What can I do to make it faster?
reply: Check the disk is not full (under 10% free slows Windows badly), then cut what starts with the machine: Task Manager > Startup, and turn off the things you do not need. If it has a spinning hard drive, swapping it for an SSD is the single best £40 you can spend; adding RAM helps if you always have many tabs open.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what are some basic composition rules I should follow.
reply: Make the shape, not the whole outfit: black leggings and a black top read as almost anything, then one thing does the work - a cardboard box for a robot or a rocket, a bin bag and a belt for a cape, a paper plate and elastic for a mask, a stripy top and an eye patch for a pirate. Paint it the night before, not the morning of, and ask the party's theme first.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how to clean his ears. Can you help me?
reply: An ear that smells, hurts or makes him shake his head is usually an infection or ear mites, and a vet needs to look down it with an otoscope and give drops that match the cause - the wrong drops can burst an eardrum. Don't push cotton buds down it or use old drops from last time, and hold off the bath until it is clear.

instruction: I'm interested in sports. What are some popular sports?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for ways to exercise at home. What are some good options?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different types of trains.
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: I'm new to the company and I'm trying to figure out my commute options. Does the company offer a shuttle service?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm a stamp collector and I was wondering how to find out how much my collection is worth.
reply: Chipping in is a shared cost split between the people it is for, so the fair default is the same amount from everybody: whoever is organising works out the total and how many people are covering it, and the rest pay that share. In practice that is a fiver or a tenner for an office collection, ten to twenty pounds for a wedding, a big birthday or a leaving do from people who know them well, and more than that is a personal choice, not an expectation.

instruction: I'm due for my annual check-up and I was wondering what I should expect.
reply: Ask for a bigger rope in the language of their worry: "Give me the report for two weeks and I'll send you the summary on Friday. If it is wrong, we go back to daily checks." Name one thing you will deliver and one date, then deliver it - hovering usually comes from a manager who was caught out before, and evidence retires it faster than a complaint.

instruction: I'm looking for information about music awards. What's the biggest music award show?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I've been feeling really anxious lately, and I was wondering if you had any tips for managing it.
reply: Treat it as information before it is a battle: something at school is usually behind it - a friendship, a lesson, a child or a teacher - so ask the teacher for the pattern of the days they refuse. Keep the morning calm and small (clothes out the night before, one step at a time), get them through the gate even for a short day, and ask the GP about anxiety if it goes on for more than a fortnight.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas to decorate my living room. What are some popular decorative accessories?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my math homework and I don't know who to ask for help.
reply: Underline what the question actually asks, then write down the numbers it gives you and what units they are in. Guess the answer roughly before calculating - if your working is far off the guess, the sum is wrong, not the guess.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into exercise and I was wondering what's a good way to start.
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm planning a train journey from London to Manchester. What's the approximate travel time?
reply: Go the weekend after a bank holiday, or in the shoulder season, and book the train three or four weeks ahead with a railcard - it usually costs less than the petrol. Stay one town out from the famous one and travel in: a twenty-minute train is a few pounds and the same room is half the price.

instruction: I need to convert 30 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit.
reply: Celsius freezes water at 0 and boils it at 100; Fahrenheit puts the same two marks at 32 and 212, so a Fahrenheit degree is the smaller one. To convert, multiply the Celsius figure by 1.8 and add 32 - body heat is 37C or 98.6F, and a hot day is 30C or 86F.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. What are some popular museums I should visit?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm interested in martial arts. What are some popular martial arts disciplines?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm a football coach and I'm looking for some strategies to improve my team's defense. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for ideas to decorate my living room. What are some popular fabrics for upholstery?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about jazz music. What is jazz?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who's a rising star in the NBA?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: Is it going to snow today?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I cut my finger while cooking. What should I do?
reply: Hold the knife in a pinch grip - thumb and forefinger pinching the blade where it meets the handle, the other three fingers round the handle - which lines the blade up with your forearm and gives you control. On the other hand, curl the fingertips under so the knuckles lead and the flat of the blade rides against them, because that is what keeps fingers clear rather than watching them.

instruction: I'm interested in archery. What is the key to achieving precision in archery?
reply: Change nothing but the aim: same stance, same grip, same speed every throw, elbow up, and a follow-through that finishes with your hand pointing at the target. Practise in blocks - 20 darts at treble 20, then 20 at the doubles round the board, and always finish on a double.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas for a weekend staycation. What are some popular activities to do locally?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm a big fan of the Boston Red Sox. What year did they win their first World Series?
reply: The Boston Tea Party was a protest on 16 December 1773, when colonists dressed as Mohawks dumped 342 chests of taxed tea from three ships into Boston harbour. Britain closed the port in reply, and the two sides were at war within eighteen months.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for an online learning platform to use with my students. Have you heard of Google Classroom?
reply: For essays, video calls and Netflix, almost anything current works: 8GB RAM, a 256GB SSD and a 14 inch screen, around £400 to £550. A Chromebook is fine if everything lives in Google Docs, but avoid it for a course that needs Windows software.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something sporty. What types of sports are popular?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm worried about endangered species. What's the main reason why animals become endangered?
reply: A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals: a fox, an owl and a lion are predators, and the animals they eat are their prey. Predators keep prey numbers in check, which is why removing them can upset a whole habitat.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some good rescue organizations?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to demonstrate math concepts to my students. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask them to show you the first step they'd try, then work one example together and let them do the next alone: that's the bit that teaches. If they're stuck on why, not how, draw it; almost every school maths idea has a picture (a bar for fractions, a graph for equations).

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV, but I want to compare prices before I buy. Do you know if Best Buy matches prices from other stores?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm interested in sports. What are some popular sports in the United States?
reply: The United States has 50 states, plus Washington DC, which is a federal district rather than a state. Alaska and Hawaii are the two outside the mainland.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What kind of camera is best for a beginner?
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different types of food. What's a popular Japanese dish?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: What do bears do during the winter?
reply: Hibernation is a way of getting through a season with no food: the animal's temperature, heart rate and breathing drop, and it lives off the fat it laid down in autumn. A bear's heart can slow from 40 beats a minute to 8, and a hedgehog turns almost cold to the touch.

instruction: What is the place value of the 5 in the number 456?
reply: Place value is what a digit is worth because of where it sits: in 4,582 the 4 is four thousands, the 5 is five hundreds, the 8 is eight tens and the 2 is two ones. The same digit means different things in different columns, which is why 0.5 is five tenths and 0.05 is five hundredths.

instruction: I'm trying to create a budget for my shopping expenses. Can you tell me how to start?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my social studies homework. What is geography?
reply: Keep the sentences short and the geography simple: who is where, what is in reach, and what each of them wants in the next ten seconds. Two or three blows that land badly, one thing that goes wrong - a foot in a puddle, a hand that will not close - and a cost at the end, because a fight nobody loses anything in reads like a dance.

instruction: I'm a student and I'm having trouble deciding what subjects to take in school. What are some popular art subjects?
reply: Pick the subjects you will still work at on a bad week, then check the entry requirements for two or three courses you might want later, because that is what closes doors rather than the subjects themselves. Keeping one essay subject and one numerical one keeps more options open than people expect.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I don't know how to use the treadmill.
reply: A treadmill is not bad for you: the deck gives a little more than pavement does, and the machine keeps the pace honest. It is a touch easier than running outside because there is no wind or camber, so set the incline to 1% to make it match the road, and run tall rather than holding the handles.

instruction: Is it going to rain today?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I want to learn about steaming food. What is steaming?
reply: A bain marie is a pan of simmering water with a bowl sitting in it, so what is in the bowl is heated by steam and never by flame: chocolate melts without seizing, custard and hollandaise thicken without curdling, and a sauce stays warm without catching. The bowl must not touch the water and the water must not boil hard - steam is gentle, a rolling boil splashes and scorches.

instruction: I'm interested in smart glasses. What are they used for?
reply: The optometrist tests your eyes and writes the prescription; the dispensing optician makes and fits the glasses. Most high-street shops are both, so you see whoever your appointment is with.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding next weekend and I need a new outfit. What should I wear?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm concerned about climate change. How does it affect agriculture?
reply: A biome is a large region with one climate and the plants and animals that go with it: rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, coral reef. The same biome turns up on different continents, because it is the climate that decides it.

instruction: I'm going to a birthday party this weekend and I'm not sure what to get my friend. What's a good gift idea?
reply: Ask the host if there is anything they need, then bring something they can use that night: a bottle of something they drink, a soft drink if you are not sure, or a pudding or cheese for the table. For a housewarming, a plant or a nice tea towel lasts longer than another candle.

instruction: I'm hungry, what are some popular breakfast meats?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm learning about life cycles in school and I was wondering, what's the life cycle of a butterfly?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I've been wondering about light in technology. What are some uses of light?
reply: Light is a form of energy that travels as a wave and also as particles called photons, at about 300,000 km a second in a vacuum. It carries colour, lets us see, and is only a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

instruction: I have a big family with lots of siblings. What do you think is a good way for siblings to bond?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas on pet toys for my cat. I want to keep her engaged and active.
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for a new car stereo system. What are some popular brands?
reply: Small, petrol, and as dull as you can bear: a hatchback like a Corsa, Fiesta, Polo or Yaris with a small engine. Check two things before the car itself - the insurance group, because a 1.0-litre in a low group can cost half what a bigger car costs to insure, and the MOT history on gov.uk for gaps and advisories.

instruction: I'm interested in set design for theater productions. What are some common materials used for building sets?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's a popular song right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my video calls. The background is very distracting. Is there a way to change it?
reply: Check Settings > Battery for the app using the most: social and video apps in the background are usually it, so restrict background refresh and turn the screen brightness down. If the phone is two or more years old, have a look at battery health, because a worn battery drains no matter what you switch off.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to make my lectures more engaging for my students. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Open with a story about one day at that school, not with a thank-you list, and keep the whole thing to three minutes: the story, what it taught you, then the one sentence you want people to remember. Say it out loud standing up four times before the day, and put the last line on a card in your hand - a rehearsed ending is what makes a speech land.

instruction: I'm going to ride the subway for the first time. Is it safe?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. What are some common problems with guitars?
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: I'm planning a family movie night. Do you have any movie suggestions for kids?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What kind of music do you like?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm interested in astronomy and I was thinking of buying a telescope. What's the difference between a refractor and a reflector telescope?
reply: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface: the ray hits the surface and leaves at the same angle on the other side of an imaginary line straight up from it. A smooth surface such as a mirror reflects the rays in one direction and gives a clear image; a rough surface scatters them and gives a duller, softer one.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for family holiday traditions. What are some popular ones?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I love animals, especially dogs. Do dogs dream?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm interested in languages. How many languages are there in the world?
reply: Pick by what you will actually use it for, not by which is easiest on paper: the language of the country you visit, or of the family you are marrying into, beats any ranking. With no reason to choose, Spanish is the usual bet - about 500 million speakers, spelling that matches the sound, and a lot of cheap material - and if you already have French or Italian, the other one of the pair is the cheapest start of all.

instruction: I'm feeling a bit stiff from sitting at my desk all day. Do you have any suggestions for some simple stretches I can do?
reply: See a physio if the pain has lasted more than a fortnight, keeps coming back, or comes with numbness, weakness or pins and needles - and you can refer yourself on the NHS without seeing a GP first. If it is a recent strain that is already easing, gentle daily stretching plus some strength work (sit-to-stands, bridges, a short walk) is what a physio would give you anyway.

instruction: I'm worried about my online privacy. What's the best way to keep my data safe on social media?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account. Private means new people have to ask to follow you, but it does not hide anything from the people already following, so check that list too.

instruction: I'm trying to save money, but I keep buying things I don't need. Do you have any advice?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm looking for a vacation destination. What are some popular cruise destinations?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. Who are some famous athletes that were inducted into the Hall of Fame recently?
reply: Neil Armstrong (1930-2012) was the American astronaut who took the first steps on the Moon on 20 July 1969, on Apollo 11. His line as he stepped down, about one small step and one giant leap for mankind, is one of the most quoted sentences of the century.

instruction: I'm excited for the Summer Olympics. When do they take place?
reply: Late March to early April, moving north as the season goes: Tokyo usually peaks around the end of March, Kyoto a few days later. Book accommodation months ahead, and be flexible, because a cold spring can delay it by a week or two.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my summer wardrobe. What are some popular colors for summer fashion this year?
reply: For a sunny border: lavender, salvia, verbena, sedum, rudbeckia, cosmos and a grass or two give colour from June to October and take the heat. Plant in spring or early autumn and water them well through their first summer, because that is what makes them drought-proof later; after that, a mulch in spring is most of the work.

instruction: What causes day and night?
reply: Night is simply the side of the Earth turned away from the Sun: with no sunlight to scatter, the sky is dark. The stars are there all day too, but the bright blue scattered light drowns them out.

instruction: I'm having trouble keeping my plants watered. What's the best way to water them?
reply: Group the pots together out of the wind, mulch the compost with gravel or bark, and stand them in a saucer so the water that runs through soaks back up. A big pot dries out far slower than a small one, so pot up rather than watering more, and in a heatwave check them morning and evening - a pot whose roots fill it can want water twice a day.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy snack option. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening as a hobby. What are some common garden pests I should watch out for?
reply: Earthworms are most of it: a badger can eat well over a hundred in a night, which is why a lawn full of small conical holes is badger work rather than a pest. The rest is beetles and grubs, slugs, roots, windfall fruit, and now and then eggs or a chick, plus anything a bin bag offers.

instruction: I'm trying to decide whether to use a mobile app or a web app for a new project. What's the main difference between the two?
reply: An app is a program built for a phone or tablet, installed from the store that came with the device - the App Store on an iPhone, the Play Store on Android. It runs on the phone itself and keeps its own data, so an app and the website of the same name can hold different things, and deleting the app usually takes its data with it.

instruction: I'm looking for some new home cooking shows to watch. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I have a dog and a cat at home. Who should take care of them when I'm away?
reply: Keep the house the way they know it: the furniture where it is, the food, water, bed and litter tray in the same spot, and the same routine for walks and meals. Say their name before you touch them so they are not startled, leave a light on in the room they sleep in, and a radio on low gives them something to steer by.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed lately and I'm looking for some mindfulness practices to help me relax.
reply: Meditation is paying attention to one thing on purpose - usually the breath - and coming back to it each time you notice you have drifted; an empty mind is not the aim, and the noticing is the skill. The tested versions are the eight-week courses, MBSR and MBCT, mainly for low mood and anxiety.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my spring wardrobe. What are some popular colors for spring fashion this year?
reply: For a sunny border: lavender, salvia, verbena, sedum, rudbeckia, cosmos and a grass or two give colour from June to October and take the heat. Plant in spring or early autumn and water them well through their first summer, because that is what makes them drought-proof later; after that, a mulch in spring is most of the work.

instruction: My washing machine isn't working. What could be the problem?
reply: Warm on the outside after a hot wash is normal, so a washer or dryer that is only a little warm and works fine needs nothing. What is not normal is a plug, socket or cable that is hot, a burning smell, a door glass too hot to touch, or the machine tripping the fuse: switch it off at the wall, unplug it and get it looked at rather than using it again.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Can you tell me about sleep schedules?
reply: The routine matters less than the regularity: same time, lights down, screens off, and something calm for the last half hour, like a shower, a few pages of a book or the dishes. Keep the bed for sleeping, and if you are not asleep in 20 minutes get up and read somewhere dim until you are sleepy.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I'm looking for some tips.
reply: Make the first session tiny and today: open the topic list, pick the one you know least, and test yourself on it for ten minutes, because starting is the part that is failing rather than the studying. Then put three short sessions in the week you actually have, each ending with a self-test instead of a reread, and give each one a stopping time so it cannot drift to midnight.

instruction: I'm looking for some discounts on summer clothing. Do you know if there are any sales going on?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm planning a last-minute trip to Paris. What's the weather like this time of year?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I heard it's going to snow this weekend. Is that true?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm looking for sports drinks to replenish electrolytes after my workout. What are some popular options?
reply: A sports drink is water with sugar and salt, and it only earns its place in a long or hot session: over about an hour, or two sessions in a day, or a match in the heat. For an ordinary gym hour, a 5k or a swim, water is enough - a 500ml bottle of sports drink is about 30g of sugar, and the salt you lose is replaced by the next meal.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. What are some common sleep disorders?
reply: Long sleeps now and then are just a debt being paid, especially after a run of short nights. Needing nine or ten hours most nights and still waking flat is worth a GP visit: an underactive thyroid, low iron, low vitamin D, depression and sleep apnoea all show up that way, and each is easy to test for.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to keep my vitamins and supplements organized. Do you have any storage ideas?
reply: One folder or box for each thing you actually have to keep — tax, home, car, health — and one tray for this month. Open the post standing up, over the bin, and deal with each letter once: pay it, file it, or ring the number on it, because a second read is how the pile grows.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for interactive simulations?
reply: *The Hobbit* is the easiest way in, *Mistborn* by Brandon Sanderson if you want a big magic system to learn, and *Piranesi* by Susanna Clarke if you'd rather have something short and strange. All three are fine for adults and teenagers.

instruction: I'm a big fan of LeBron James. What sports does he play?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. Is global warming real?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to an amusement park this weekend. What's the best food to try there?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris and I'm looking for affordable accommodations. What's the difference between a hostel and a hotel?
reply: Book direct with a small hotel or guesthouse once you know roughly where you want to be: a phone call often beats the price on the booking site, and it is the cheapest way in small towns. Hostels and apart-hotels win for a week, and a kitchen saves more than a lower nightly rate.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family about important decisions. Do you have any tips?
reply: Decide what you actually want from the conversation before you start it - an apology, a change, or just to be heard - and ask for that rather than for the whole history. Pick one recent thing and say it plainly: 'When you rearrange my plans without asking, I feel about ten years old.' Pick a short visit or a walk rather than a long sit-down, and leave the subjects that never move alone.

instruction: My phone's battery life is really bad. Is there a way to make it last longer?
reply: Switch on Low Power Mode and the phone will last hours longer: Settings > Battery on an iPhone, or Battery saver in Android's settings. Turn the screen brightness down, drop 5G to 4G if that is a setting you have, and ask in the nearest cafe, library or shop to plug into a socket for fifteen minutes - a short top-up is fine for the battery.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my professional skills, particularly my creativity. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different types of theater. What's the main difference between a musical and a play?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable payment devices. What are some popular types?
reply: For work, four things decide it: the fabric, the rise, the length and the pockets. A wool-poly blend or a cotton twill with a little stretch creases less and gives when you sit and stand; a mid rise that sits at the waist stays put through a shift; and the hem should break once on the shoe, so buy the length that fits you - short and petite lengths are sold off the rail and cost no more than a tailor.

instruction: I want to start batch cooking to save time during the week. What are some good meals to start with?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm looking for unique accommodations. What are some options?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm a student and I'm having trouble deciding what subjects to take in school. What are some popular subjects?
reply: Pick the subjects you will still work at on a bad week, then check the entry requirements for two or three courses you might want later, because that is what closes doors rather than the subjects themselves. Keeping one essay subject and one numerical one keeps more options open than people expect.

instruction: I'm thinking of going on a cruise. What's the best time of year to go?
reply: An equinox is the day the sun sits over the equator, so day and night are about twelve hours each everywhere: around 20 March and 22 September, which is when spring starts on one half of the planet and autumn on the other.

instruction: I'm hungry, what's a popular breakfast food?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping this weekend. Do you have any coupons I can use?
reply: Buy for the first night, not for the shelves: a takeaway voucher for the evening the boxes are still out, a box with loo roll, tea, milk, mugs, bin bags, a corkscrew and a phone charger, or a hot meal you turn up with. A plant, a good bottle or a decent set of tea towels all last longer than another candle, and a voucher for a hardware shop is the unromantic one people are pleased about.

instruction: I'm looking for information about government jobs. What are some main categories of government jobs?
reply: The government runs the country day to day - the prime minister, the cabinet and their departments - and parliament makes and checks the laws. The government sits inside parliament, so the same people are in both, and the roles are opposite: ministers propose, and parliament scrutinises, its own backbenchers included.

instruction: I'm trying to improve my job performance. What are some key factors that can help me?
reply: Two sentences: your job title and what you actually do in a week, then one thing you have changed or finished. "I am a warehouse team leader - I run a shift of eight, and I have just moved us onto scanners, which cut picking errors." Thirty seconds is plenty; they are testing whether you can be brief and whether the last job taught you anything.

instruction: I'm interested in learning how to code. Have you heard of Codecademy?
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: I'm craving something sweet. What are some popular types of desserts?
reply: Sweet: honey or jam with a spoon of peanut butter, stewed apple with cinnamon, or frozen berries stirred in while it is hot. Savoury: butter, salt and a poached egg, or grated cheese and black pepper - porridge is only oats cooked in water or milk, so it takes either, and the salt is what makes the sweet version taste of something.

instruction: I'm worried my pet isn't getting enough exercise, especially on rainy days when we can't go for a walk.
reply: Shade and water out all day, walk before ten and after five so the pavement is not burning his pads - if it is too hot for your hand for five seconds, it is too hot for his feet. Never leave him in a parked car, even with the windows down: it reaches 40C inside in ten minutes.

instruction: I'm looking for a new T-shirt. What's a popular style right now?
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable cameras. What are some popular types?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: What is buoyancy?
reply: Buoyancy is the upward push a liquid or gas gives anything in it, equal to the weight of the fluid it pushes aside. A steel ship floats because the air inside makes it push aside more water than the ship itself weighs, while a solid lump of steel cannot.

instruction: I'm looking for some educational resources for my child. What are some good websites for learning?
reply: *The Hobbit* is the easiest way in, *Mistborn* by Brandon Sanderson if you want a big magic system to learn, and *Piranesi* by Susanna Clarke if you'd rather have something short and strange. All three are fine for adults and teenagers.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the countryside and I'm looking for a cozy place to stay. What's a bed and breakfast?
reply: Make up the best bed and plan one shared outing a day, so the flat is mainly for sleeping and everyone gets a reason to leave it. Agree meal times on the first evening and keep one evening for yourself; the stay goes better when nobody is guessing.

instruction: I'm looking for a new belt to go with my jeans. What type of belt is popular right now?
reply: The four-in-hand is the one to learn: put the tie round your neck with the wide end hanging about 30cm lower, cross it over the narrow end, take it up through the loop at your neck, then wrap it across the front and up through the loop again, and pull it down through the knot you just made. Draw it up snug and slide the knot where you want it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new workout routine. What's a good dance fitness class for beginners?
reply: Wear what you can dance in for hours and don't have to hold: dark jeans or a dress with shoes you can stand in. Check the club's own rules first, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the beach this weekend, but I heard there might be a wind storm. What's the weather forecast looking like?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm looking to upgrade my computer's RAM. What type of RAM do I need to look for?
reply: RAM stands for random access memory: the working space a computer keeps open programs in, wiped when it loses power. More of it helps when many tabs or programs are open at once; it does not make a single program faster, and a full disk is the more common reason a computer feels slow.

instruction: I'm trying to cook some vegetables, but I'm not sure what method to use.
reply: Fry them into a hash: chop them small, start with an onion and a pinch of salt, and let them crisp at the edges before you add anything wet. Roasted vegetables are better through pasta with garlic and a spoonful of the cooking water, and anything soft goes into soup with stock and a blender.

instruction: I'm looking for a new movie to watch. What are some popular movie streaming services?
reply: *Happy Valley* for tense British crime, *The Bear* for short, intense episodes, or *Detectorists* if you want something gentle and funny. All three are easy to watch with a partner.

instruction: I have a new puppy and I'm not sure what vaccinations he needs.
reply: A cough that lasts more than a day or two needs a vet, and quickly if the animal is flat, off its food or breathing fast; kennel cough is common in dogs and spreads where dogs meet. Don't give human cough medicine, and keep a coughing dog away from others until the vet has seen it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What are some popular author events happening soon?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smart thermostat for my home. What's the main benefit of having one?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I've been thinking about walking more.
reply: Walking alone will not do it - what you eat decides most of it - but 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day is a fair target, and the gain is that it burns a little and keeps you from sitting down all day. The quicker half is the plate: a smaller portion of the starch, more protein and vegetables, and no drinks with sugar in.

instruction: I'm going to graduate soon. What is the significance of wearing a graduation cap and gown?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What are some examples of simple machines in everyday life?
reply: A turbine is the jet's opposite: wind pushes the blades, the blades turn a shaft through a gearbox, and a generator turns that spin into electricity. The blades are long and thin because the force goes up with the square of their length, and the machine feathers them out of the wind when it is too strong to use.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm trying to improve my technique. What's the most important thing to focus on?
reply: Pick your corner before the run starts, keep it low and side-foot it inside the post, and do not change your mind on the last step: a firm, repeatable penalty beats a clever one. Practise ten to the same corner at the end of training so the run, the plant foot and the strike are one habit.

instruction: I have a home recording studio and I'm having trouble with echo. What can I do to reduce it?
reply: In the call settings pick the right microphone and speaker instead of the default, because a monitor or headset often takes them over. Raise the input volume to about 80%, sit closer to the mic, and use headphones on both ends to stop the echo; if it is an older relative, a tablet is easier than a phone.

instruction: I'm looking for a snack. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: I'm trying to decide on discipline methods for my kids. What do you think about time-outs?
reply: Keep instructions under twenty seconds, show it once, then let them try it in a game — children learn by playing, not by queueing to take turns. Give every child a job or a ball, praise the one who does the thing you asked, and change the game every ten minutes.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about sports. What are some popular sports?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I have a lot of devices in my home. What is the main difference between a router and a modem?
reply: The router is the box that joins your home network to the line from your provider and gives every device in the house its own address, so they can find each other and the internet. A modem is the part that speaks to that line; most homes now have both in one box, which is why turning it off and on fixes so much.

instruction: I'm looking for a classic movie to watch tonight. What's a popular one from the 80s?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. What's the difference between a chord and a scale?
reply: A kitchen scale weighs in grams, which is how most baking is written and the only way to be sure of flour, butter and sugar - a cup of flour varies by a third depending on how it is scooped. Put the bowl on, set it to zero, and add each thing in turn.

instruction: I want to start cooking healthier meals but I don't know where to begin. Can you give me some general tips?
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my summer wardrobe. What are some popular colors for this season?
reply: For a sunny border: lavender, salvia, verbena, sedum, rudbeckia, cosmos and a grass or two give colour from June to October and take the heat. Plant in spring or early autumn and water them well through their first summer, because that is what makes them drought-proof later; after that, a mulch in spring is most of the work.

instruction: I want to start meal planning to reduce food waste. What are some basic steps I can follow?
reply: Let it cool, pour it into a bottle or a tub, and put that in the general waste - never down the sink, where it sets with wipes into a blockage. A little fat can go in the food waste caddy if your council collects one, and a recycling centre takes larger amounts of used cooking oil.

instruction: I'm looking for some new casual wear for summer. What's popular this year?
