reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm looking to return a product I bought online, but I'm not sure about the return policy.
reply: Changed your mind? Bought online, by phone or by post, you have 14 days from the day it arrives to say so and another 14 to send it back, for any reason, and the refund covers the standard delivery.

instruction: I'm looking for gift ideas for my sister's birthday.
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I burned my hand on the stove, what should I do?
reply: Hold the knob in for twenty seconds after the flame catches, then let it go: a pilot that won't hold is nearly always the thermocouple, a small part a Gas Safe engineer swaps in ten minutes. A draught or a dirty jet does it too, and both mean taking the case off, so that is their job as well.

instruction: I'm going to New York City for the first time and I want to know more about the subway system. Can you tell me about the subway map?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are the steps to adopt one?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with my family. What's a classic board game that's fun for everyone?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: What is gravity?
reply: Gravity is the attraction between anything with mass: the Earth pulls you toward its centre, and you pull the Earth back by the same rule. Bigger mass means a stronger pull, which is why the Moon orbits the Earth and the Earth orbits the Sun.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to balance my work and family life. I've heard of job sharing, but I'm not sure what it is.
reply: It means just about coping - keeping up with money, work or everything at once. Which one is it for you?

instruction: I'm looking for some new dinner ideas. What's a popular international dinner food?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm looking for a new casual dress for the weekend. What's a popular style right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my daily commute easier. I'm tired of driving to work and dealing with traffic.
reply: Giving up driving is three jobs, and doing them in this order makes it much easier. First the official side: if the reason is medical, tell the DVLA, because a licence you should not be using is not valid for insurance, and tell your insurer either way.

instruction: I'm concerned about the apps on my phone. What kind of permissions do they usually ask for?
reply: On an iPhone it is Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions: turn it on, then set the age rating for apps, block in-app purchases, and require a passcode for installs. On Android install Google Family Link and approve apps and screen time from your own phone.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in food tours. What are some popular food options to try?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm worried about my dog's bad breath. What can I do about it?
reply: Don't: never make a pet sick at home. Salt water, peroxide and fingers down the throat do real damage, and for some poisons being sick makes it worse.

instruction: I'm looking for information about the new buses in town. Are they accessible for people with disabilities?
reply: A disabled person's bus pass is a council scheme and it costs nothing to apply. You qualify if you are blind or partially sighted, deaf, or cannot walk without help or can only walk a short way without severe pain, and also with a learning disability or if a driving licence was refused on medical grounds.

instruction: What's the difference between BC and AD?
reply: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus: universal because one plug replaced the pile of different ports a computer used to have, and bus because several devices share it. The letter after it is the shape - USB-C is the small reversible one - and the number is the speed, so a blue USB 3 socket copies much faster than a black USB 2 one.

instruction: I'm looking for upcoming music festivals in my area. Can you help me?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for something new to watch. Do you have any sports documentary recommendations?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm learning about magnets in school. What is an electromagnet?
reply: A magnet has a magnetic field, and it pulls on materials whose electrons can line up with that field, like iron, nickel and cobalt. Cut a magnet in half and you get two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different painting techniques. Can you tell me about watercolor?
reply: White spirit for oil-based gloss, water for water-based paint, and only a little: about one part white spirit to ten parts paint, stirred in rather than shaken, and no more than about a tenth of water in emulsion or water-based gloss. More than that and the paint stops forming a film, so it dries patchy and the sheen goes.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a lever?
reply: A lever is a bar that turns on a pivot, and it lets a small push move a big weight if the pivot sits close to the weight: a crowbar, a wheelbarrow, a see-saw and a bottle opener are all levers.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. What is a foster family?
reply: Ask two things before you take a side: why now - smaller, cheaper, the stairs, or to pay for care - and what date they are working to, because those decide everything else. If any of the money is coming your way, get it written down what it is: a gift, a loan or an advance on what you would inherit, and who agreed it.

instruction: I'm trying to improve communication with my family. What are some ways to do that?
reply: For a family with an older parent, WhatsApp is the easiest: install it, add the contacts, then tap New group, name it and pick the people. Turn on their notifications for that one chat and pin it to the top of their screen, and start by sending a photo so there is something to reply to.

instruction: I'm going to a concert tonight and I'm really excited. I love the lighting at concerts.
reply: Light tells your brain it is still daytime, so keep the room as dark as you can: a blackout curtain or an eye mask, and turn the lamp off rather than dimming it. If a streetlight gets in, a curtain that reaches the floor helps.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow and I need a ride. Do you know if Uber is available in my area?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm looking to improve my flexibility through yoga. What are some beginner-friendly poses I can start with?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm looking for a snack. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: I have a pest control problem at home. I've seen some ants in my kitchen.
reply: Wipe the trail away with vinegar and water and put bait down close to it: they carry the bait back to the nest and that is what kills the colony, so do not spray the line they are following. Give the bait a week or two: the ants keep coming for the first few days and then the stream thins out and stops.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Fix the wake-up time first: the same hour every day, including after a bad night, and the rest tends to follow within a fortnight. Then the three that do most of the work - daylight and a walk in the first hour, no caffeine after lunch, and a screen-free half hour before bed - and only get into bed when you are sleepy rather than tired.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. I've heard of plein air painting. What is it?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: What is the Roman numeral for the number 5?
reply: Place value is what a digit is worth because of where it sits: in 4,582 the 4 is four thousands, the 5 is five hundreds, the 8 is eight tens and the 2 is two ones. The same digit means different things in different columns, which is why 0.5 is five tenths and 0.05 is five hundredths.

instruction: I'm learning about light in my science class. What is reflection?
reply: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface: the ray hits the surface and leaves at the same angle on the other side of an imaginary line straight up from it. A smooth surface such as a mirror reflects the rays in one direction and gives a clear image; a rough surface scatters them and gives a duller, softer one.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of pastries?
reply: Hot chocolate sauce, tinned peaches or raspberries with a splash of their juice, crushed biscuits or toasted nuts, and a pinch of salt on anything caramel. A shot of espresso over vanilla is affogato, which is the best 30-second pudding there is.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up in the morning. What are some natural ways to wake up?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. What are some popular tourist attractions?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I'm thinking of adding some living space to my home. What are my options?
reply: Keep rent to about a third of your take-home pay, and add council tax, energy and water before you commit. Multiply the rent by 12 and check you can also cover a five-week deposit and the first month up front, because those two land together.

instruction: I'm feeling really down lately and I don't know what's wrong with me.
reply: Do one small thing you used to enjoy today, at half enthusiasm, because mood follows action more often than it arrives on its own: a walk to the shop, a phone call, ten minutes of a game you liked. Then stack the three things that lift a low mood most reliably - daylight within an hour of waking, 20 minutes of walking, and one person you really talk to rather than message - and keep bedtime and meals at the same time, because a sad week wrecks both and then feeds itself.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for the first time. What should I expect?
reply: Ask the vet for a nurse appointment and wait in the car until it's your turn, then feed him treats in the waiting room without letting other dogs crowd him. Ask them to crouch down and examine him on the floor, and go in for a free weigh-in every few weeks so most visits are boring: a dog who has been in four times for nothing is a much easier patient.

instruction: I want to learn sign language. What's the most common sign for 'hello'?
reply: One emoji, only where the tone is already warm: a thumbs-up or a smile in a work chat is fine, a string of them rarely is. Skip faces in anything to a client, in bad news, and in a first email to someone senior; a plain "Thanks!" or a short "Sounds good" carries the warmth without the risk.

instruction: I'm thinking of taking a daily multivitamin, but I'm not sure if I should also take a separate vitamin D supplement.
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I'm looking for a new video game to play. What's popular right now?
reply: Match it to the age and the room rather than to the adverts. Under about ten, a Nintendo Switch is the safe first console: it comes with a game, works handheld or on the television, and Nintendo's free parent app sets a daily limit and turns it off at bedtime.

instruction: I love watching sports, especially baseball. What's it like watching a game at a stadium?
reply: Pick the team someone you already watch with supports, or the one nearest to where you live — going to games matters more than the badge. Watch a few matches first and let it happen; supporting a team is mostly habit plus the people you watch it with.

instruction: I'm a big fan of Elvis Presley. What year did he release his first single?
reply: Martin Luther King Jr (1929-1968) led the American civil rights movement without violence: the Montgomery bus boycott in 1955, the 1963 March on Washington, and the laws of 1964 and 1965 that ended legal segregation and barred the poll tax. He was shot in Memphis in April 1968.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals. What are some superfoods I can add to my recipes?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I want to start lifting free weights. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Learn five movements and ignore everything else for a month: squat, hinge (deadlift), push, pull and carry. Two or three sessions a week, three sets of 8–12, adding a little weight each time.

instruction: I'm learning about ecosystems in school. What are some examples of biotic factors?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy snack option. What do you suggest?
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: I'm looking for some information on eco-friendly fashion. What does that mean?
reply: Smart and modest is the safe read: trousers or a skirt past the knee, shoulders covered, and shoes you'd wear to a nice lunch. Take a layer, because old buildings are cold.

instruction: I'm looking for information about movie production. What's the main role of a film director?
reply: The producer is the person who shapes the recording: the arrangement, the sounds, how the parts fit, and the mix at the end. They are not the songwriter and not the engineer.

instruction: I'm trying to create a website, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm new to yoga and I'm looking for some beginner poses. Can you tell me about some basic ones?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthier way to cook vegetables. What's steaming?
reply: Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces, toss them with oil and salt and roast at 200C (180C fan) for 30 to 40 minutes, turning once. Give them space on the tray; a crowded tray steams instead of roasting.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my career. What are some popular courses for career development?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I've been feeling really stressed out lately and I'm not sure what to do about it.
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What do plants need to survive?
reply: Soil holds a plant up and holds the two things it needs: water around the roots and the minerals it cannot make itself, like nitrogen for leaves and phosphorus for roots. Plants can grow without it only if someone feeds them those minerals in water, which is how hydroponics works.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into exercise and I was wondering what's a good routine for a beginner.
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm new to yoga and I'm not very flexible. Is yoga still good for me?
reply: Not for injury, no: strength work and building up slowly are what keep you off the physio's couch, and a stretch before sport takes a little power off it. What the flexibility is worth having is the reach - a high shelf, a shoe, getting up off the floor - and that goes quickly if you stop.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make learning more interesting. What are some popular visual aids that can help?
reply: Draw what is in front of you, not from memory: a mug, your own hand, the chair opposite. Ten minutes a day beats a long session at the weekend, one object a day for a fortnight, and use a soft pencil (2B) on cheap paper so you are not afraid of it.

instruction: I'm going to a black-tie event and I'm not sure what to wear.
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with friends. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook.

instruction: I'm planning a trip and I need to buy train tickets. Can you help me with that?
reply: Coaches are the cheapest way between two cities: booked two or three weeks ahead a long trip is often under 20 pounds when the train is over 60, and the overnight coach saves a hotel night as well. Book on the operator's own site or app, take the ticket on your phone, and put the big bag in the hold, which is included but has to be tagged.

instruction: I'm planning to renovate my bathroom and I'm looking for some ideas.
reply: A new bathroom is usually £3,000 to £7,000 fitted, and £8,000 to £12,000 with the bath moved, the walls tiled and the plumbing changed. Tiling and moving the toilet or the bath account for most of the difference.

instruction: I'm feeling overwhelmed with work and struggling to find time for my hobbies. Do you have any work-life balance strategies?
reply: Mostly it is the setup, not willpower: enough sleep, food, the phone in another room and one thing open at a time. Work in 25-minute blocks on a single task written down first, because choosing where to start is half the distraction, and stand up for the break.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to advance my career. What are some common goals people set for career development?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm a bit confused about the difference between the metric system and the imperial system. Can you explain it to me?
reply: An empire is one state ruling other peoples and places beyond its own borders, usually taken by force and governed from the centre; a kingdom is one country under a king or queen. Empires rarely last more than a few hundred years, because the parts stop needing the centre.

instruction: I'm looking for dinner ideas. What are some common dinner entrees?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm thinking of adopting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping this weekend. What's in season right now?
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer.

instruction: I was just thinking about my grandparents and the stories they used to tell me when I was a kid. What kind of stories did your grandparents tell you?
reply: Ask about their day in small pieces rather than 'how are you': what they had for breakfast, who they sat with, what is on the noticeboard. Take in one bit of news from outside - the weather, a grandchild, the garden - and do something side by side instead of talking face to face: a hand of cards, a photo album, the crossword.

instruction: I'm planning to go grocery shopping this weekend. What are some popular items to buy at a farmer's market?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow and I need a taxi. What's the best way to get one?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is condensation?
reply: Condensation is water out of the air landing on a cold surface: the windows and the outer corners are wet in the morning, it clears when the room is aired, and it comes back on cold days. A leak is a patch that grows and stays wet whatever the weather, and rising damp only runs along the bottom metre of a wall, usually with a tide mark.

instruction: What is the capital of Australia?
reply: Sydney has about 5.3 million people, the biggest city in Australia.

instruction: I'm looking for sustainable fashion brands. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm going shopping for new clothes this weekend. What should I consider when buying a new shirt?
reply: Buy one pair of dark trousers in the size that fits you now and one plain shirt, this week rather than on the morning: those two do more for how you look than an expensive jacket that does not button. Ask for the trousers to be taken up while you are in the shop.

instruction: What is the light/color spectrum?
reply: Light is a form of energy that travels as a wave and also as particles called photons, at about 300,000 km a second in a vacuum. It carries colour, lets us see, and is only a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my science homework. Can you tell me about photosynthesis?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm having trouble with screen sharing during video calls. Can you help me?
reply: On an iPhone, Screen Mirroring in Control Centre sends the screen to a smart TV, and in a FaceTime or WhatsApp call the share button does it inside the call. On Android it is Cast or Smart View in the quick settings, and Zoom, Teams and Meet each have Share Screen once you are in a meeting.

instruction: I'm trying to reduce my impulse buys when I go shopping. Do you have any tips?
reply: Take the biggest single line first and halve it rather than cutting it out: bought coffee and lunches are usually the largest and easiest, and going from five a week to two saves more than cancelling a handful of small subscriptions. Set a weekly limit for that one thing and stop when it is gone.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation and migration in school. What is adaptation?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm trying to create a daily cleaning routine. What are some tasks I should include?
reply: Ten minutes a day beats one big clean: pick a fixed time - before bed is the easy one - and do the surfaces in one room and the washing-up, so nothing piles up. Give everything a home, a box, a hook or a shelf, and anything without one goes out.

instruction: I'm looking for some fun pet toys for my dog. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: Our school is having a science fair next week. What kind of projects do you think would be good for it?
reply: Don't try to answer the whole of it at once. Write three short lists: what you are good at (the things other people ask you for, not what you would like to be good at), what you would do for free, and what you need money for.

instruction: I'm looking for some new clothes, but I'm not sure if I should go for a local brand or a global one.
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sport to play. What are some popular sports for casual players?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for ways to reduce my daily commute costs. I've heard carpooling is a good option.
reply: Anything wholly and necessarily for the work: stock and materials, tools, software and subscriptions, insurance, bank fees, the business share of your phone and broadband, travel between jobs (not the commute), and a share of the heating if you work at home. Keep the receipt and note what it was for.

instruction: I have a puppy and I'm not sure what kind of food to feed him.
reply: Keep it plain and small: plain chicken with boiled rice, or his own food, in four or five small meals a day rather than one big one. Withhold food for a few hours first if he has been sick, keep the water down, and skip anything fatty or milky.

instruction: I'm learning about rugby and I was wondering, what is a scrum?
reply: A scrum restarts play after a knock-on or a forward pass: the eight forwards of each side bind together and push against the other pack, the scrum-half feeds the ball into the middle, and the hooker strikes it back with a foot. The side that shoves the other back can win the ball against the head.

instruction: What's the difference between the equinox and the solstice?
reply: An equinox is the day the sun sits over the equator, so day and night are about twelve hours each everywhere: around 20 March and 22 September, which is when spring starts on one half of the planet and autumn on the other.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about recycling. What are some common materials that can be recycled?
reply: Book a bulky waste collection with your council - most charge twenty to forty pounds and collect from the doorstep - or take it to the recycling centre, where it is stripped for its springs. Charity shops rarely take one for hygiene reasons, so a free-ad site is the other realistic route if it is clean and you say collection only.

instruction: I'm thinking of switching my dog to a raw diet. Is that a good idea?
reply: It can be done well and it is not automatically better. A raw diet has to be properly balanced; minced meat on its own is short of calcium, it carries more bacteria than cooked food, and a puppy needs the right ratio of calcium to phosphorus for its bones to grow right.

instruction: I'm interested in trying yoga. What are some popular yoga styles?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I'm not sure where to start. Can you help me create a workout plan?
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm interested in playing the guitar, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school, and I was wondering how genetics affect our everyday lives.
reply: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions for making one thing the body needs, usually a protein: eye colour, blood type and how a muscle works all come from genes. You inherit half your genes from each parent, and they switch on and off depending on the cell.

instruction: I'm having trouble telling time. Can you help me?
reply: The same hour in the same order every night: screens off 45 minutes before bed, the lights down, and three small things done the same way - teeth, tomorrow's clothes out, ten minutes of a book. Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet, and put the phone on charge in another room, because the check at 11pm is what stretches the hour.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New Zealand and I'm looking for some adventure activities.
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. Do you think they would like a family gathering for the holidays?
reply: Do the inviting yourself, and make it the same thing each week - a walk on Tuesday, a coffee on Saturday - because a standing date is easy to say yes to and does not need them to suggest anything. Ask specifically and name the day, ring rather than text, and keep asking after a no, since the first answer from someone lonely is often no.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What makes a bedroom comfortable for sleep?
reply: A bedroom around 16 to 18C suits most people for sleep: cool enough that you need a duvet, not so cold you wake up. Cracking a window for ten minutes before bed, a lighter duvet in summer and a hot water bottle rather than a hot room all help, and a warm bath an hour before bed sends you to sleep faster than a warm bedroom does.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, what kind of exercise does it need?
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my manager at work. What are some ways to improve our working relationship?
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to network with other professionals in my industry. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: The first three clients come from people who already know your work: a former employer or colleague, a friend who runs something, the local shop, a group you are already in. Pick one service you can name in a sentence, then tell twenty people you have started and what you charge - not a general announcement, one message each.

instruction: I'm worried about air pollution in my city. What are the main causes?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in our oceans. Is it really a big problem?
reply: Plankton is the mass of tiny plants and animals drifting in water that cannot swim against the current: the plant sort makes oxygen and feeds everything up to the whales. Half the oxygen you breathe was made by it.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What's the difference between a carnivore, an herbivore, and an omnivore?
reply: A carnivore is an animal that eats other animals: a lion, a cat, a heron, a spider. Most have sharp teeth or a beak for tearing meat, and a short gut, because meat is easier to digest than plants.

instruction: I'm learning about matter in school. What is matter?
reply: Dark matter is the name for mass we cannot see but can measure: galaxies spin and bend light as if they hold far more matter than the stars show. Nobody yet knows what it is made of, which is why it is one of the big open questions.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for some friends, but they all have different tastes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm looking for information about fast fashion brands. What are some popular ones?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the local mall this weekend. What's the history of shopping malls?
reply: The Roaring Twenties were the 1920s in America: jazz, cinemas, cars, radios and short skirts, on borrowed money and with drink banned by Prohibition. It ended with the Wall Street crash of October 1929 and the Depression that followed.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my parents. They're getting divorced and I'm not sure how to deal with it.
reply: Don't try to be the parent yet: be a reliable adult who is not in charge of the rules and let their actual parent do the discipline for a while. Keep the offers small and repeated - a lift, a snack they like, a show you both watch - because loyalty to the other parent is usually what is behind the hostility.

instruction: I've always been curious about how mountains affect the culture of people living near them. Can you tell me a little bit about that?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet. What are some benefits of having one?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for new sandals. What are some popular types?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm having trouble understanding electrostatic force. Can you explain it to me?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: What's the difference between a minute and an hour?
reply: A football match is two halves of 45 minutes, with 11 a side including the keeper, and the clock keeps running — it does not stop for injuries or substitutions. The 90 minutes is why teams time-waste, and why added time at the end of each half can be long.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what's the difference between acids and bases.
reply: A base is the opposite of an acid: it takes hydrogen ions, turns red litmus blue, and reacts with an acid to make a salt and water. An alkali is a base that dissolves in water, such as baking soda or bleach.

instruction: I'm looking for a new music streaming app. What are some popular music streaming apps?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I love going to the mall to look at the seasonal displays. What's your favorite season for window shopping?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm planning to visit an amusement park with my family soon. What are some basic safety tips we should follow?
reply: Decide in advance what you will do and how long you will stay, and tell people early so nobody is surprised on the day. Have one safe topic and one exit ready ('we need to get the little one home'), and step outside for ten minutes when it heats up.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I want to try progressive muscle relaxation. What is it?
reply: Either, and it does not matter much: a couple of minutes on a tight spot before you train loosens it enough to move better, and afterwards it feels good without doing much for soreness. What works is slow passes over the muscle, 30 to 60 seconds a spot, breathing out and stopping at a 6 or 7 out of 10 rather than gritting your teeth.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip from New York to California and I was wondering if there's a way to carpool for long distances.
reply: Assume there is something round the next bend - a tractor, a horse or a walker - so drive at a speed you could stop from within what you can see, which on a hedge-lined lane is often 30mph or less. On a single-track road use the passing places: pull in on your left to let oncoming traffic through, and do not park in one.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any tips for better sleep quality?
reply: Fix the wake-up time first: the same hour every day, including after a bad night, and the rest tends to follow within a fortnight. Then the three that do most of the work - daylight and a walk in the first hour, no caffeine after lunch, and a screen-free half hour before bed - and only get into bed when you are sleepy rather than tired.

instruction: I'm planning a dinner party for some friends and I'm not sure what to make.
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan. What's the best time to visit?
reply: Late March to early April, moving north as the season goes: Tokyo usually peaks around the end of March, Kyoto a few days later. Book accommodation months ahead, and be flexible, because a cold spring can delay it by a week or two.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What type of books do you recommend?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: I'm learning about science in school and I'm having trouble understanding atoms and molecules. Can you explain the difference?
reply: A molecule is two or more atoms joined together: two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen make a water molecule, and DNA is a very long one. The atoms can be the same, as in oxygen gas, or different, as in water.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, and I want to know if agility training is good exercise for them.
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my dental care routine. What's the best way to brush my teeth?
reply: Most bad breath is bacteria on the tongue and between the teeth, not the stomach: brush twice a day, clean between the teeth once a day, and gently brush or scrape the back of the tongue. Drink water through the day, because a dry mouth is the other common cause, and cut back on coffee, alcohol and smoking.

instruction: I'm looking for a new tennis racket. What's a good brand?
reply: Club tennis is won by keeping the ball in, so play the percentages: height over the net and length to the back of the court, and count how many cross-court balls you can rally without missing - 20, then 30. Two sessions a week of that beats a new racket.

instruction: I'm planning to do some deep cleaning at home and I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Ten minutes a day beats one big clean: pick a fixed time - before bed is the easy one - and do the surfaces in one room and the washing-up, so nothing piles up. Give everything a home, a box, a hook or a shelf, and anything without one goes out.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school. What is heredity?
reply: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions for making one thing the body needs, usually a protein: eye colour, blood type and how a muscle works all come from genes. You inherit half your genes from each parent, and they switch on and off depending on the cell.

instruction: What's the current wind speed outside?
reply: A dry, breezy day dries a normal load outside in two to four hours, and a cold sunny day with wind is nearly as good as a warm one, so 8C and breezy beats 20C and still. Rain, fog and damp evening air put the water back, so bring it in before dusk.

instruction: I'm looking for information about pet grooming services in my area. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: A dog groomer is usually £30 to £60 depending on the size and coat, with a hand-strip or a matted coat costing more. Ask what happens if your dog is matted, because some charge by the hour to sort it out, and book four to six weeks apart for a coat that keeps its shape.

instruction: What is a yo-yo?
reply: It's rhythm: r-h-y-t-h-m, with no vowel between the y and the t. It is one of the few English words where y does the vowel's job.

instruction: I cut my hand while cooking. What should I do?
reply: Hold the knife in a pinch grip - thumb and forefinger pinching the blade where it meets the handle, the other three fingers round the handle - which lines the blade up with your forearm and gives you control. On the other hand, curl the fingertips under so the knuckles lead and the flat of the blade rides against them, because that is what keeps fingers clear rather than watching them.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about subways. When was the first subway system built?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I heard it's going to be really cold this weekend. Is that true?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding what I read. Do you have any tips for me?
reply: Read the questions before the passage, so you know what to look for. Then read once for sense and go back to the lines the questions point at, quoting a few words in your answer.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to the beach next week. What should I pack?
reply: Take a warm mid layer and a waterproof shell, plus long sleeves rather than vests - even in June the evenings drop to about 8C. Add a hat and gloves if you are going high or out on the water, and midge repellent for anywhere damp and windless in high summer.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I bring?
reply: Take your medicines in their boxes, the admission letter, phone and charger, and loose clothes you can get on one-handed; for a day case add slippers with a back and a named bag for your clothes. Leave valuables at home, and ask the ward what they provide before you pack towels and toiletries.

instruction: I'm worried about my dog. He's been vomiting a lot. Should I take him to the vet?
reply: One vomit or one loose poo in a dog that is otherwise bright is usually nothing: withhold food for a few hours, then offer small amounts of plain chicken and rice, and keep the water down. Ring the vet if it repeats, if there's blood, if he is flat and not drinking, or if it is a puppy, an old dog or going on for more than a day.

instruction: I like music and I'm trying to learn more about it. What's the difference between a melody and a harmony?
reply: A solvent is the liquid something dissolves in, and the thing that dissolves is the solute: water is the usual solvent, while white spirit and acetone dissolve things water cannot, like paint and nail polish.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of construction jobs. What are some main categories?
reply: A builder is usually £150 to £300 a day for one person, or £200 to £350 for two, and the big jobs are priced as a whole rather than by the day. Scaffolding, skips, and any work that needs building regulations add to it, and a quote should name all three if they apply.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sports club to join. What sports do most clubs offer?
reply: Search for the sport plus your town and 'club', then email and ask about a taster session: most clubs have a beginners' or social night that costs a few pounds. Turn up to that rather than a match, and say you're new — clubs are used to it, and it's the fastest way to find people at your level.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape, so I was thinking about starting a strength training program. What are the benefits of strength training?
reply: It's worth it even in 20 minutes: two sessions a week of squats, press-ups, lunges and a row with a band or dumbbell builds real strength. Muscle matters for everyday things like carrying shopping and climbing stairs, not just for looks.

instruction: I'm interested in track and field events. What's the most popular one?
reply: Put the dates on a blank timeline you draw yourself, and group them around a few anchor events you already know. Then link each new date to a story or a person rather than a bare number, and test yourself by covering the dates and filling them in.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school. What is the main job of the circulatory system?
reply: An organ is a part of the body made of several tissues working together for one job: the heart pumps blood, the lungs take in oxygen and the liver cleans the blood. Your skin is the largest organ, and organs work together in systems.

instruction: I was wondering, how do animals communicate with each other?
reply: Meet on neutral ground, one walker each, and walk them side by side rather than face to face, then let them off lead only in a fenced space where the older dog can walk away. At home give the older dog his own bed, bowl and corner that the puppy cannot reach, feed them apart, and step in before the puppy hangs off his ears.

instruction: I'm looking for some fashion tips for the upcoming fall season. What are some popular colors this year?
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms to improve my skills. Have you heard of LinkedIn Learning?
reply: Pick the one thing you can already do that people pay for, and sell it in the smallest packet: tutoring a GCSE subject, fixing bikes, editing CVs, dog walks on the way home, weekend cover in a bar or care home. Sell to people you can reach this week rather than building a website, do two or three paid jobs before you spend anything on it, and keep a record of what you earn: £1,000 a year of side income is tax free (the trading allowance), and above that you register for Self Assessment.

instruction: I'm looking for a new mobile shopping app. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Write down every purchase for a month, or let your banking app sort it into categories. The surprises are nearly always takeaways, subscriptions and small card taps, and seeing them once is what makes cutting them easy.

instruction: I'm moving to a new city with a very hot climate. What can I do to adapt?
reply: Loose, light cotton in a pale colour is the coolest thing to wear, because it lets air through and reflects the sun; a wide hat and sunglasses are worth more than another layer of sunscreen. Keep shoulders covered over a long day and wear shoes you can walk in on hot tarmac.

instruction: I'm feeling tired all the time. Do I need more sleep?
reply: Most constant tiredness is dull rather than medical: too little sleep, a late screen, alcohol, caffeine after lunch, or no daylight. Give it two weeks of the basics before you assume anything else - the same bedtime and getting-up time every day, twenty minutes outside in the morning, no caffeine after two, and no phone in the bedroom.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise bike for my home gym. What should I consider when choosing one?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm learning about plate tectonics in school. What are the Earth's plates?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I'm a huge music fan. I've been to a few concerts and I was wondering what it's like backstage.
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I was wondering what the temperature is like today.
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about folk music. What is folk music?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy breakfast option. What's a good choice?
reply: An egg is one of the cheapest good foods there is: about 78 calories and 6g of protein, with the B12 and vitamin D that people buy supplements for. The cholesterol in food turned out to matter far less than the saturated fat in the diet, so one or two a day is fine for most people.

instruction: I'm going to a music festival this weekend. What are some popular festival activities?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking for outdoor concerts in my area this summer. Do you know of any?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm trying to figure out my personal style, but I'm not sure where to start. Can you tell me a little bit about color analysis?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I heard it snowed last night. How much snow fell in my area?
reply: Snowed under just means buried in work or messages - nothing to do with weather. What is the pile in front of you?

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about cultural exchange programs?
reply: One person, one language works well - you always in one, your partner in the other - and the rule that matters is that each language gets real, daily use rather than lessons. Expect the school language to win once they start, so keep books, cartoons and relatives in the other one.

instruction: I'm looking for a new rug for my living room. What types of rugs are popular right now?
reply: Go bigger than feels right: in a living room the rug should reach under the front legs of the sofa, so about 160x230cm for a small room and 200x290cm behind a three-seater, and a bedroom rug wants to run at least 60cm past each side of the bed. Wool wears and cleans better than polyester and does not flatten as fast; a thick underlay makes a cheap rug feel expensive and stops it creeping.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I couldn't find the model I want in local stores. Can I buy it online from another country?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm trying to set up a home gym, what equipment do I need to get started?
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm looking for some new hobbies to try in my free time. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm looking for some new ideas to update my family's traditional recipes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm going to the mall this weekend and I love window shopping. What do you think makes a store's window display attractive?
reply: Paint it all one pale colour, ceiling included, and put a mirror where it catches a window: the eye reads the reflection as another room. Hang the curtains at ceiling height rather than at the window, keep the floor visible, and use one rug that stops short of the walls rather than carpet that runs wall to wall.

instruction: I'm looking for a simple no-cook recipe for a snack.
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for new music to listen to. What are some popular music streaming services?
reply: Worth it if you work or stream at home, more than one person uses the connection, or you game: a phone hotspot will do for one light user, but its data cap and the delay on a video call show up fast. 5g home broadband sits between the two - no line and no engineer, but check the coverage at your postcode and how it holds up at 8pm before you take a two-year deal.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated. What are some water-rich foods I can eat?
reply: Water with a meal is fine: it does not dilute your stomach acid enough to matter, and it helps if you eat fast or get constipated. The only thing to watch is filling up on it so there is no room for the food - a glass or two rather than a pint before you sit down.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a pet, what are some popular pets?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: What are the main TV awards?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas on what to do during my lunch break at work.
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. Do I need to tune it every time I play?
reply: Nine times in ten it is the strings: new ones stretch for a week, so tune up, bend every string a little, and tune again - three or four times the first evening. Old strings go dead and stop holding pitch, so if they are more than a few months old, change them.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any suggestions for improving my bedroom environment?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: Our school is having a book fair next week. What is a book fair?
reply: Ask four or five people, not a crowd, and fix the next date before the first meeting ends - a club that meets every six weeks at a set day keeps going, one that waits for everyone to be free does not. Pick short books to begin with, let whoever chose it lead for ten minutes, and bring one question rather than a summary: "who did you believe?", "what would you have done?".

instruction: I'm interested in learning about adaptation to extreme environments. Can you give me some examples?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm looking for a new blender. What are some popular brands?
reply: A blender is a tall jug with blades in the base, for things that pour - smoothies, soup, sauces. A food processor is a wide bowl with a blade and discs, for chopping, slicing and grating solid food like onions, nuts or pastry.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any bedtime routine recommendations?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering about the states of matter.
reply: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, with a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. Atoms join into molecules, and everything you can touch is made of them; they are mostly empty space.

instruction: I'm planning to shop online for some gifts. What are some popular online payment methods?
reply: Use a virtual card: most banking apps make a one-off card number in a few taps, so the shop never holds the real details, and set a low limit on it. Where that is not offered, one card kept for online only, notifications on for every payment, and the real one frozen in the app between uses - most let you unfreeze it in seconds.

instruction: What's the date today?
reply: It means deciding as you go instead of planning now. What is the day?

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay fit at home, I don't have any equipment.
reply: For two or three nights: one change of clothes plus a layer, one pair of comfortable walking shoes, toiletries in a bag, phone charger and any tickets. Roll clothes to fit more in, and leave the "just in case" outfit at home.

instruction: I'm planning a retirement party for my mom. What are some common family celebrations?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I want to bake a cake, but I don't know how to make the frosting.
reply: Rub a thin film of butter or flavourless oil all round the inside with a piece of kitchen paper. A cake tin also wants a dusting of flour, tapped round and the extra tipped out, or a lining of baking parchment on the base; a pan or a roasting tin wants only the oil, wiped on while it is cold.

instruction: I'm looking for some new ideas for family recipes. What's a popular dish that families often make together?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for some fun seasonal activities to do with my family. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking to improve my professional skills. What's the most important one to focus on?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm looking to buy a new laptop online, but I'm not sure which one to choose.
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm learning about animal life cycles in school. What is a life cycle?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. Can you tell me about jazz?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about World War II. What caused it?
reply: World War Two began in Europe on 1 September 1939, when Germany invaded Poland; Britain and France declared war two days later. Japan had already been at war with China since 1937, and the United States joined in December 1941 after Pearl Harbor.

instruction: I love sunny days, what time does the sun rise today?
reply: The exact time depends on where you are and the date, so I cannot give you the clock time: a weather app or the Met Office page for your postcode has it, along with tomorrow's. Sunrise moves only a minute or two a day, but the gap between sunrise and sunset swings by hours across the year.

instruction: I'm interested in sustainable communities. What is a sustainable community?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I'm having trouble finding things in the store. Do they have a standard layout?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm planning to cook for my family this weekend, but I've never cooked for so many people before. Do you have any tips?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm looking for some gift ideas for my friend's birthday. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: What are the most popular gaming platforms right now?
reply: A console is cheaper and simpler: it plays everything at good quality for years, no upgrades, and you can sell it on. A gaming PC costs more up front but gets cheaper games, higher settings and mods, and doubles as a work machine - so pick the console for a shared living room and the PC if you already sit at a desk with a monitor.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm planning a Career Day event for my students. Do you have any suggestions for guest speakers?
reply: Ask about their day in small pieces rather than 'how are you': what they had for breakfast, who they sat with, what is on the noticeboard. Take in one bit of news from outside - the weather, a grandchild, the garden - and do something side by side instead of talking face to face: a hand of cards, a photo album, the crossword.

instruction: I'm worried about my job performance. What are some key factors that affect it?
reply: Two sentences: your job title and what you actually do in a week, then one thing you have changed or finished. "I am a warehouse team leader - I run a shift of eight, and I have just moved us onto scanners, which cut picking errors." Thirty seconds is plenty; they are testing whether you can be brief and whether the last job taught you anything.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sofa for my living room. What types of sofas are popular right now?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I have a lot of homework due tomorrow and I'm feeling overwhelmed. How do I prioritize my tasks?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm planning my nephew's Bar Mitzvah celebration. What's the significance of this event?
reply: It is what people say to someone before a show or a match: it means good luck, because wishing it out loud is thought to jinx it. What are you going on for?

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear during the summer. What fabrics should I look for?
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.
