instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of chickens. What comes first, the chicken or the egg?
reply: Hens lay them. Each one starts as a yolk released from the hen's ovary, which picks up the white and then the shell on its way down the oviduct, roughly one egg every 25 hours in a good laying hen.

instruction: I'm looking for some new cabinets for my living room. What types of cabinets are available?
reply: Second-hand furniture is the best value there is, and charity shops and Freecycle are the places to look. Check for woodworm holes, sagging cushions and smoke smell, and measure your door and stairs before you collect anything big.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get around the city without a car. What are some options?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I want to bake a cake, but I'm not sure what kind of flour to use.
reply: A cake rises on three things - the air you beat in, the bubbles the raising agent makes, and steam - and when it does not, the culprit is nearly always baking powder past its date (a teaspoon per 150g of plain flour, or use self-raising), the flour beaten in too hard once it went in, or the oven door opened in the first 20 minutes. Cream the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, fold the flour in with a spoon, fill the tin two-thirds full, and bake at 180C (160C fan) without opening the door.

instruction: I'm curious about parenting styles. What are some common types?
reply: Don't try to be the parent yet: be a reliable adult who is not in charge of the rules and let their actual parent do the discipline for a while. Keep the offers small and repeated - a lift, a snack they like, a show you both watch - because loyalty to the other parent is usually what is behind the hostility.

instruction: I'm looking for a new kitchen gadget. What's the most useful one you'd recommend?
reply: A trivet is the stand that keeps something hot off the table or the counter - a pan, a casserole, a slow cooker's pot. Wooden, cork, stone or metal, all it does is hold the heat away from the surface; a folded dry towel does the same job when the trivet is not there.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a new smartphone. What's the difference between Android and iOS?
reply: An app is a program built for a phone or tablet, installed from the store that came with the device - the App Store on an iPhone, the Play Store on Android. It runs on the phone itself and keeps its own data, so an app and the website of the same name can hold different things, and deleting the app usually takes its data with it.

instruction: I'm looking for a quick snack recipe. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Butter first, then something sharp or salty on top: peanut butter and sliced banana, mashed avocado with salt and lemon, beans with a dash of Worcestershire, or a tin of sardines on hot toast. Cheese on toast under the grill for 3 minutes is the fastest good one, and a sliced tomato under the cheese stops it going dry.

instruction: I have a lot of homework to do and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Can you help me organize it?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm having trouble with writing. Do you have any tips?
reply: Slow down by about a third for a week and use lined paper: most messy handwriting is speed, not hand shape. Then pick the two or three letters you join badly (r, n, m and your a's) and copy a paragraph a day, ten minutes, saying each letter as you write it.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm interested in learning more about project-based learning. What is it?
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm a big fan of Tom Brady. What did he do after retiring from football?
reply: The Great Famine was Ireland's potato blight years, 1845 to 1852. About a million people died of hunger and disease and another million emigrated, so the population fell by roughly a quarter and never recovered.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, especially for my heart. Do you have any heart-healthy recipes?
reply: You can eat well without cooking if you build the plate from the shop: a bag of salad or a punnet of tomatoes, ready-cooked chicken or a tin of tuna or chickpeas, and bread, couscous or a microwave pouch of rice. Frozen veg straight from the microwave is the cheapest half-plate of vegetables there is, and a pot of yogurt with fruit is pudding.

instruction: I'm looking for natural cleaning solutions for my home. What are some alternatives to chemical-based cleaners?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm getting ready for summer and I want to know what I should do to get my home ready.
reply: Decide in advance what you will do and how long you will stay, and tell people early so nobody is surprised on the day. Have one safe topic and one exit ready ('we need to get the little one home'), and step outside for ten minutes when it heats up.

instruction: I'm planning to do some exterior home maintenance this weekend. What's the most important thing to do first?
reply: Decide in advance what you will do and how long you will stay, and tell people early so nobody is surprised on the day. Have one safe topic and one exit ready ('we need to get the little one home'), and step outside for ten minutes when it heats up.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What are some popular ones?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm planning to make a salad for lunch. What are some popular vegetables I can use?
reply: Bean and alfalfa sprouts are the one salad thing to be careful with: they are grown warm and damp, which is exactly what bacteria like, and rinsing does not remove what has got inside the seed. Eat them cooked - stir-fried or dropped into soup for a minute - and if you want them raw, buy a bag that says ready to eat and keep it cold.

instruction: I'm looking for information about cultural festivals. Can you tell me about Diwali?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for a new camera lens. What types are there?
reply: A pair of glasses is usually £100 to £300 with standard lenses, and varifocals or thin lenses push it to £300 to £500. The frame is where the money goes, and the two-for-one offers usually mean two pairs of a cheap lens.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in school and I'm a bit confused about potential energy. Can you explain it to me?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of salmon. What is the first stage?
reply: Four to six weeks, with a test kit telling you when it is done. Ammonia from fish waste and food has to be eaten by bacteria that take weeks to grow, and the tank is ready when ammonia and nitrite both read zero a day after you add a little food: ammonia peaks in the first week or two, nitrite in the third or fourth, and nitrate climbing at the end is the sign it has finished.

instruction: I'm looking for information about school buses. What is the main purpose of a school bus?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: How are the Chicago Cubs doing this season?
reply: Bats sleep upside down, hanging by their feet, and many hibernate through the winter that way. Hanging upside down means a fall is a drop of a few centimetres, and taking off is just letting go.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I don't know what to wear. Can you tell me about traditional wedding attire?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I have two cats and a dog, and sometimes they fight. Why do you think they do this?
reply: Separate the things they share before anything else: two bowls in different rooms, two litter trays and a high place each, so neither cat can be cornered, and a Feliway plug-in in the room they use most. Then feed them on either side of a closed door and swap their bedding, and only put them together when the hissing at the door has stopped - never face to face to sort it out.

instruction: I'm interested in CrossFit. What is it?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: What's the weather like in New York today?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to advance my career. What are some good ways to network?
reply: Try the smallest real version first: an evening course, one freelance job, or a sideways move inside your current employer. Talk to three people doing the job now and ask what the bad days are like, not the good ones.

instruction: I'm planning a family gathering this weekend and I want to do something fun with my kids. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Do one thing you could not do with them in the house and one thing that is only rest, and put the fun one first, because the tidying can wait until Sunday evening. The first night can feel strange and quiet, and that is normal rather than a sign anything is wrong.

instruction: I'm looking for something fun to do with friends. What's a board game cafe?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I want to get stronger. What are some good exercises for building strength?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris and I'm looking for a boutique hotel. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Book direct with a small hotel or guesthouse once you know roughly where you want to be: a phone call often beats the price on the booking site, and it is the cheapest way in small towns. Hostels and apart-hotels win for a week, and a kitchen saves more than a lower nightly rate.

instruction: I'm planning to start a small garden in my backyard. What plants are easy to grow for a beginner?
reply: Grow what gives you a lot from a little: salad leaves, radishes, spring onions, dwarf beans, cherry tomatoes, chillies, one courgette plant, herbs in a pot by the door, and strawberries in a basket. Go upwards where you can - beans and cucumbers up a frame, tomatoes in a grow bag - and sow a few seeds every three weeks rather than everything at once, so you eat from June to October instead of facing a glut in August.

instruction: I'm worried about my grandmother falling at home. What are some common fall hazards?
reply: Falls are usually several small things adding up rather than one bit of clumsiness: leg strength and balance, eyesight, blood pressure that dips on standing, medicines, and the house itself - which is why the second one is worth acting on rather than waiting for the third. Ask the GP for a falls review: they check blood pressure lying and standing, go through the medicines, and can refer to a falls clinic or a strength and balance class, which is what actually cuts falls.

instruction: I'm setting up my home and I want to make sure I have a first aid kit. What are the essentials I should include?
reply: A home kit is a box you can use one-handed in the dark: plasters in a few sizes, sterile gauze and tape, a crepe bandage, small scissors, tweezers, disposable gloves, a thermometer, and children's paracetamol with the dose worked out by weight. Add an ice pack, antiseptic cream and the 111 number, then check it once a year and replace anything past its date.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow and I need a ride. What are my options?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm looking to shop online, but I'm not sure if I can get items shipped to my country.
reply: A letter or a card just needs the right stamp and the full address; a parcel needs a customs form, at the counter a CN22 (a CN23 once the value is over a few hundred pounds), naming what is inside, its weight and its value - that is what the receiving country works its duty and tax out from, so write the truth rather than gift. Price goes by weight band: a small parcel to Europe is roughly £10 to £20 and outside Europe more, so weigh it first and compare a courier once it is over 2kg.

instruction: I need some motivation to start working out. Can you give me a motivational quote?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming concerts in my city. Are there any big events happening soon?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner tonight, but I'm not sure what type of protein to use. What are some popular options?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in my science class. What are the main types of energy?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm looking for some easy meal ideas. What's a one-pot meal?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for a routine check-up. What can I expect?
reply: Ask the vet for a nurse appointment and wait in the car until it's your turn, then feed him treats in the waiting room without letting other dogs crowd him. Ask them to crouch down and examine him on the floor, and go in for a free weigh-in every few weeks so most visits are boring: a dog who has been in four times for nothing is a much easier patient.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my computer's operating system. What's the difference between Windows and macOS?
reply: The operating system is the layer between the programs and the machine: Windows, macOS, Android and iOS are the four you meet. It manages the files, the screen and the battery, and it decides which apps can run, which is why an app that has stopped being updated eventually stops opening on a new version.

instruction: I'm looking for information about famous artists. Can you tell me about Vincent van Gogh?
reply: Vincent van Gogh (1853-1890) was a Dutch painter whose The Starry Night, Sunflowers and self-portraits are among the most recognised pictures in the world. He sold almost nothing in his lifetime, cut off part of his own ear in 1888, and died at 37, with his fame arriving afterwards.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby and I'm interested in gardening. What are some good plants for beginners?
reply: Plant for the whole season rather than one week: lavender, oregano and marjoram in summer, buddleia for July and August, sedum and ivy flowers for September. Leave a sunny corner of long grass and a patch of nettles, because that is where they lay, and put out a shallow dish of water with a few stones in it.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I heard about the Feynman Technique. What is it?
reply: It means doing something quickly and cheaply by skipping the careful parts. Are you being asked to, or did someone do it to you?

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming concerts in my area. Do you know any good venues?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I want to get more exercise, what are some popular sports?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm looking for a shopping mall near my place. Can you tell me about the nearest mall?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm learning about mountains in school. How are mountains formed?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I'm thinking of making homemade pet food for my dog. Is that a good idea?
reply: It can be done well and it is not automatically better. A raw diet has to be properly balanced; minced meat on its own is short of calcium, it carries more bacteria than cooked food, and a puppy needs the right ratio of calcium to phosphorus for its bones to grow right.

instruction: I want to learn about sautéing. What is it?
reply: A saute pan has straight, fairly high sides and a wide flat base: enough floor to brown without crowding, enough wall to hold a sauce or a braise. It is the pan for a risotto, a curry or a chicken joint browned and then finished in the oven.

instruction: I'm planning to buy a new car and I was wondering what the speed limit is on highways.
reply: The national limits for cars are 30mph where there are street lights (unless signed otherwise), 60mph on a single carriageway and 70mph on a dual carriageway or motorway. They are a ceiling, not a target: on a narrow country lane 40mph is often too fast for the bends, and a lower sign overrides the national limit.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new dog and I'm not sure what kind of food to buy.
reply: Put the food in a slow feeder bowl or scatter it across a towel so he has to work for it, split the day's food into three or four small meals, and use bigger kibble if he is on dry food. A dog that gulps also swallows air: with a deep-chested breed, take him to the vet straight away if his belly is swollen and he is retching and can't settle, because that is bloat.

instruction: I'm trying to learn new vocabulary for my language class. I've heard of spaced repetition, but I'm not sure what it is.
reply: Learn seven to ten words at a time, out loud, and test yourself instead of reading the list: cover the English side and say the word, then swap. Put each new word in a short sentence you would actually say, and go back over yesterday's words for two minutes before adding new ones — spacing is what makes them stay.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hat. What are some popular types of hats?
reply: Three thin layers beat one thick one: a base layer, a jumper and a windproof coat, so you can take the middle off indoors. Cover the neck, ears, wrists and ankles, which is where the cold gets in, and keep your feet warm with a thicker sock or a boot rather than a second pair of tights.

instruction: What is a second in time measurement?
reply: A pendulum is a weight on a string that swings to and fro at a steady rate, which is how clocks kept time for three hundred years: a longer string swings more slowly, and the weight hardly matters.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for ways to make my classroom more engaging for my students.
reply: Show it once, then watch them do it once, then let them do it alone with you a few feet away: most of what looks like slowness is a step nobody said out loud. Write the five or six steps on one page they can keep, do the same fifteen minutes at the same time each day rather than a long session on Friday, and ask them to explain it back to you before you decide it has not gone in - if they cannot explain it, the teaching missed rather than the learner.

instruction: What is the most popular social media platform?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account. Private means new people have to ask to follow you, but it does not hide anything from the people already following, so check that list too.

instruction: I'm looking for some DIY home decor ideas. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm trying to grow my social media presence, what are some popular platforms I should use?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm looking for eco-friendly shoes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Wear cotton or wool socks and change them daily, wash feet with soap and dry between the toes, and alternate shoes so each pair dries out. If it doesn't settle, a pharmacy antiperspirant for feet is stronger than deodorant.

instruction: I'm interested in minimalist fashion. What is it?
reply: Smart and modest is the safe read: trousers or a skirt past the knee, shoulders covered, and shoes you'd wear to a nice lunch. Take a layer, because old buildings are cold.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up in the morning. What's a good time to wake up?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm looking for a meal planning app to help me organize my cooking. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cardio machine for my home gym. What's the difference between a treadmill and an elliptical?
reply: A treadmill is not bad for you: the deck gives a little more than pavement does, and the machine keeps the pace honest. It is a touch easier than running outside because there is no wind or camber, so set the incline to 1% to make it match the road, and run tall rather than holding the handles.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into home workouts, but I'm having trouble scheduling them. Do you have any tips?
reply: Forty-five minutes to an hour is the sweet spot: five minutes of warm-up, three or four exercises at three sets each, and a couple of minutes between sets. Past 90 minutes you are mostly resting and getting tired rather than stronger, so drop an exercise rather than the rest.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking about taking a nap. Is napping good for you?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hiking trail to explore this weekend. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Go for a canal towpath, a country park or a flat riverside path: wide, level, benches along it and nothing to climb over, which is what a short walk needs. Check the surface and the slope on the site's own page before you set off, because a walk advertised as circular can still hide a stile or a flight of steps, and ring ahead if someone uses a wheelchair - big attractions, National Trust and English Heritage places among them, lend one for free if it is booked a day or two in advance.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I'm not sure what to expect. What should I do when I first get there?
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in school, and I was wondering what kinetic energy is.
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I had a weird dream last night. Do you know why we dream?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of puddings?
reply: Hot chocolate sauce, tinned peaches or raspberries with a splash of their juice, crushed biscuits or toasted nuts, and a pinch of salt on anything caramel. A shot of espresso over vanilla is affogato, which is the best 30-second pudding there is.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. Who's a famous painter I should know about?
reply: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) was an Italian painter, engineer and anatomist: the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper on one side, notebooks of flying machines and dissected bodies on the other. Fewer than twenty of his paintings survive, and it is the range of his curiosity that made him famous.

instruction: I'm looking for some home workout ideas since I don't have a lot of space.
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm concerned about the air quality in my home. What are some common sources of indoor air pollution?
reply: Most of the dust in a house is you: skin flakes and the fibres fabrics shed, plus what blows in through the windows and gets walked in on shoes. The big sources are bedding, carpet and soft furnishings, so wash the sheets at 60C every week or two and vacuum properly with a decent filter rather than a quick pass.

instruction: I have a cat named Max. He's been sick lately. What should I do?
reply: A cat that keeps being sick needs the vet rather than a wait-and-see: repeated vomiting in a cat is often a swallowed blockage (string, a hairband, a toy) or a poison, and cats go downhill fast. Offer small amounts of water, no food for a few hours, and ring the vet; go straight away if there is blood, if she is retching with nothing coming up, or if she is flat and hiding.

instruction: I'm planning to use the subway to get to work. How much does a subway ride cost?
reply: Pre-book it: the price at the barrier is often two or three times the pre-booked price for the same space, and the cheapest of all is usually a park-and-ride a few minutes out with a shuttle. Compare the total against the alternatives before you choose, because a week of parking often costs about what a taxi costs each way, and for two or three days the taxi, the train or a lift from a friend usually wins.

instruction: I heard it might snow this weekend. What are the different types of snow?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping since I moved to a new time zone. Do you have any tips on how to adjust my sleep schedule?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: What is a triangle?
reply: A triangle is a flat shape with three straight sides and three corners, and its three angles always add up to 180 degrees. By its sides it is equilateral (all three equal), isosceles (two equal) or scalene (all different); by its angles it is acute, right-angled or obtuse.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my camera. It's not taking clear pictures anymore.
reply: Clean the lens: it is a tiny piece of glass that collects fingerprints, and a dry microfibre cloth or a cotton bud with a breath on it is all it needs, never a tissue and never alcohol. Then check the camera app itself is not set to a low resolution, and that the light behind you is not the brightest thing in the frame, because a window at your back is what makes a face go dark and grainy.

instruction: I'm looking for some new cooking inspiration. Do you know any popular online cooking channels?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: What should I wear when it's raining?
reply: A waterproof with a hood is the one thing that decides the day, with a thin layer underneath rather than a thick coat, because rain gear is warm once you move. Wear shoes that keep water out - leather or a waterproof boot rather than canvas, which soaks and stays wet - and take a second pair of socks.

instruction: I'm looking for a new smartwatch. What are some popular brands?
reply: A jeweller or watch shop fits a new strap while you wait, usually £10 to £25 for a leather or silicone one, and a broken strap is always replaced rather than mended. A metal bracelet is resized by taking links out for £5 to £15.

instruction: I'm trying to track my expenses. Can you help me with that?
reply: Ask payroll or HR: digital payslips are usually in the HR or payroll portal, and a paper one is the stub or a PDF they can email. An employer has to keep the record, so they can give you a copy of any month you are missing, and a former employer's HR can usually reissue one.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What are some popular Olympic sports?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm planning to bake some cookies, but I'm not sure if I should use baking powder or baking soda.
reply: Baking soda is pure bicarbonate of soda and needs an acid - buttermilk, lemon, yoghurt - to make something rise. Baking powder is bicarbonate with the acid already mixed in, so it works with plain liquid and is what most cake recipes mean.

instruction: What is an echo?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm flying to New York tomorrow. What time should I arrive at the airport?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Broadway shows. What's currently playing?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the mall this weekend. What are some fun things to do there?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm looking for a new desk for my home office. What types of desks are popular?
reply: A laptop if you will be typing - email, essays, spreadsheets, work - and a tablet if it is mostly reading, video, calls and games on the sofa. A tablet with a keyboard costs about what a laptop does and types worse, so make it the only machine only if you truly do not type; a cheap laptop and a 300 pound tablet side by side covers the most ground for the money.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the moon phases. What are the main phases of the moon?
reply: The Moon doesn't change shape; half of it is always lit by the sun, and we see a different slice of that lit half as it orbits the Earth. A full moon takes about 29.5 days to come round again.

instruction: I have a family with kids and we are thinking of getting a pet. What are some good types of pets for families with kids?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. Do plants respond to their environment?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I want to bake something vegan. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Usually yes: cocoa, milk and cocoa butter are all vegetarian. Check the bar for gelatin in chewy or marshmallow fillings, and remember whey is fine for a vegetarian but not for a vegan.

instruction: I'm looking for a simple exercise routine to start at home. What are some good bodyweight exercises for beginners?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to exercise my dog. What are some good exercise toys for dogs?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise routine. What's a good way to get started with yoga?
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I love fall. What's the best time to see fall foliage?
reply: Take it down on Twelfth Night, 5 January, which is twelve days after Christmas - 6 January if you count Epiphany itself. A real tree is usually dropping by then anyway, and the older superstition about leaving decorations up past that night is not one to lose sleep over.

instruction: I was wondering about light and how it bends. What is that called?
reply: Refraction is light bending as it crosses from one material into another at an angle, because it changes speed: that is why a straw looks broken in a glass of water, and how a lens or a pair of glasses focuses light.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for weekend brunch. What are some popular items?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I have a cat named Max. What are some healthy foods for him?
reply: Keep it plain and small: plain chicken with boiled rice, or his own food, in four or five small meals a day rather than one big one. Withhold food for a few hours first if he has been sick, keep the water down, and skip anything fatty or milky.

instruction: What causes the seasons to change?
reply: Seasons come from the Earth's 23.5-degree tilt, not from how close it is to the sun. When your half of the planet leans towards the sun you get summer: longer days and more direct light.

instruction: I'm concerned about staying hydrated, especially for my family. How much water should children drink daily?
reply: About a litre a day for a toddler, six to eight small cups (1.2 litres) for a 4 to 8 year old, and milk plus the water in food count; under six months milk is the only drink. Leave a beaker where they can reach it, refill it without a word, and offer sips at every snack - juice or squash is one small glass with a meal, not the drink they carry all day.

instruction: I'm trying to declutter my home and get organized. Do you have any tips?
reply: Start with one room and one deadline: pack the things you use least first, label every box by room and keep one box for the first night - bedding, toilet roll, kettle, mugs, chargers, a torch and any medication. Anything you have not used in a year, sell, donate or bin it now rather than paying to move it; a bag a day from the back of a cupboard gets rid of most of it.

instruction: I'm trying to lose some weight and gain muscle, do you have any tips for that?
reply: Eat something with carbs an hour or two before if you can, and protein within a couple of hours after - a banana and yoghurt, or toast and eggs, is plenty. The order matters far less than the total: getting enough food and sleep is what makes the training work.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Are there any devices that can track my sleep quality?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris and I want to reduce my carbon footprint. Do you have any tips for sustainable travel planning?
reply: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas a person, a household or a product causes, counted in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent over a year. For a household in the UK it is roughly 8 to 10 tonnes, and the weight is not where people think: heating and electricity and car travel are the bulk of it, while a flight is big in one hit and a plastic bag is almost nothing.

instruction: I'm looking for some summer sales. Are there any good deals going on right now?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm trying to improve my vocabulary. Can you give me a word and its definition?
reply: Tell me the word and I'll spell out the sounds syllable by syllable in plain English, with the stressed part in capitals. If it is a name, I'll say it the way the person would.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my teamwork skills at work. Do you have any tips?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for something to watch this weekend. What sports are on TV?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the new shopping mall this weekend. What can I expect?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I have a brother who is 10 years older than me. What do you think are some common differences between siblings with a large age gap?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What is the greenhouse effect?
reply: Aim for 15 to 25C by day: open the vents and the door at about 25C, and shut them again mid-afternoon so the heat is kept for the night, because a closed greenhouse is 5 to 10C warmer than the air outside. Tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers stop growing below about 12C and set no fruit below 15C, so a heater set to 10 to 12C keeps them alive rather than growing, and a max-min thermometer in the shade inside tells you what your own greenhouse is really doing.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Disneyland. What are some popular rides?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm not sure what kind of food to give her.
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I want to improve my communication skills. What is active listening?
reply: A hearing aid is a microphone, an amplifier and a tiny speaker in your ear: the microphone picks up the room, the electronics boost the frequencies speech lives in and the speaker sends it down the canal louder. Digital ones split the sound into bands and turn down the background to suit the room.

instruction: What is an inclined plane?
reply: A wing is shaped so air moves faster over the top than underneath, and the pressure difference pushes the wing up; that force is called lift. Engines provide the forward thrust, and lift grows with speed until it beats the plane's weight.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school and I was wondering, what is a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the circulatory system does.
reply: An organ is a part of the body made of several tissues working together for one job: the heart pumps blood, the lungs take in oxygen and the liver cleans the blood. Your skin is the largest organ, and organs work together in systems.

instruction: I'm looking for a job in hospitality. What are some common job categories in this field?
reply: Join one real thing about them to one real thing about you: "You're rebuilding the booking system, and that's the part of my last job I liked most." Ten minutes on their website before you go is enough to sound like you mean it. Never answer with "I need a job" or with vague praise of their culture.

instruction: I'm looking for discounts on electronics. Do you have any sales going on?
reply: Check two things before you sell: the trade-in price from the network or the maker, and what the same model with the same storage sells for on a resale site - the private sale is often 20 to 30% more. Say the battery health and any marks honestly, sign out of your accounts and factory reset it in front of the buyer.

instruction: I'm a little worried about air travel safety. What are the chances of a plane crashing?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm interested in non-verbal communication. Can you tell me a bit about it?
reply: It means talking or thinking without getting anywhere. What is the decision you keep circling?

instruction: I'm looking for a new vacation destination. Can you suggest a place with a rich cultural experience?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I had a bad nightmare last night. What causes nightmares?
reply: Nightmares usually follow stress, late food, alcohol or a heavy film before bed, so start there. If the same one keeps coming back, write it down in the day and rehearse a different ending a few times: that is the technique that works.

instruction: It's really cold outside. What should I wear?
reply: Dress for ten minutes in: a thin wicking base layer, a fleece over it and a windproof shell on top - waterproof rather than thick if it is wet - so you should feel slightly cold on the doorstep and warm by the first mile. Wind is what makes it cold, so keep it out at the neck, cuffs and ankles and cover the hands and ears, which is where it bites first.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What is the Paris Agreement?
reply: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas your choices add up to in a year, counted as carbon dioxide: heating, electricity, flights, car trips, the food and things you buy. A typical UK footprint is around 10 tonnes a year, and flying and meat are usually the biggest single items.

instruction: My dog gets really anxious when I leave the house. What's going on?
reply: Dogs hear bangs far louder than we do and can't tell they are harmless, so plan the night instead of waiting for the first one: walk him before dark, then shut the windows and curtains, put the radio on and let him hide where he likes with something to chew. Stay in with him, don't take him to a display and never tell a frightened dog off; if he panics badly, ask the vet about a calming plan a few weeks ahead and check his microchip details are up to date in case he bolts.

instruction: I'm trying to save time on grocery shopping. What are some benefits of online grocery shopping?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I need to wear a suit. What's the difference between a suit and a tuxedo?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I'm having trouble balancing my work and family life. My parents are always telling me to spend more time with my kids.
reply: Take the smallest break that is really a break, and take it today: twenty minutes out of the house without your phone, or a bath with the door shut while someone else does bedtime. Then lower the bar for the rest of the day - one meal, one wash, no craft - because a worn-out parent does not need a plan, they need an hour.

instruction: What is matter?
reply: Dark matter is the name for mass we cannot see but can measure: galaxies spin and bend light as if they hold far more matter than the stars show. Nobody yet knows what it is made of, which is why it is one of the big open questions.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan. Do I need a visa?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to organize my closet. Do you have any storage solution ideas?
reply: Go up before you go out: a shelf over the door, hooks on the back of a cupboard door and boxes stacked to the ceiling use space you already have. Take the doors off one base cupboard and put a bin or open shelves in it, keep the worktop clear, and send anything you use less than monthly to the top of a wardrobe or under the bed.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately and I was thinking of taking some vitamin supplements. What are some good vitamins for energy?
reply: Most supplements are fine with most tablets: vitamin D, vitamin C, a multivitamin, cod liver oil and a probiotic can be taken alongside blood pressure tablets, statins, levothyroxine and antibiotics. The two that need care are vitamin K, which works against warfarin, and calcium or iron tablets, which want four hours between them and a thyroid tablet.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about team sports. What are some key elements of a successful team?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for some hidden gems to visit in my local area. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm going to a potluck dinner and I need a dish idea that serves a lot of people.
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm going to use a taxi for the first time. What's the usual tip for a taxi driver?
reply: Get the ride first: a bus or tram driver will wave you on, station staff let you through a barrier, and a ticket machine or the operator's app takes another card or the phone. In a taxi, the meter and a receipt are what a complaint rests on.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family's holiday feast. What are some popular dishes that people usually serve?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: What is hibernation?
reply: Hibernation is a way of getting through a season with no food: the animal's temperature, heart rate and breathing drop, and it lives off the fat it laid down in autumn. A bear's heart can slow from 40 beats a minute to 8, and a hedgehog turns almost cold to the touch.

instruction: I'm rearranging my living room furniture and I'm not sure where to put my sofa.
reply: Measure the gap and the doorway before you argue, and take the legs or the door off if that is all that is stopping it: most sofas come apart at the back. Bought online or over the phone, you have 14 days to cancel and they have to collect a bulky item, though they can charge for that if the terms say so; bought in a shop, a return is their own policy, and something made to your measurements has no right to one.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms to improve my skills. Have you heard of Skillshare?
reply: Pick the one task that slows you down most and learn just that: a 20-minute tutorial on the one thing, then use it on real work the same day. Ask your manager for the training budget by showing what it will save (a day a month, fewer errors); most budgets go unspent because nobody asks.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What colors do you think I should start with?
reply: Two coats of a decent emulsion usually cover a dark wall, and going much lighter than the old colour can need three; sand and wipe the wall down first and do not thin the paint. If the old colour is a strong red or a dark green, ask for a combined primer and undercoat tinted towards the new colour - it saves a coat and stops the old shade grinning through.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness tracker. What are some popular brands?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm feeling really thirsty after my workout. Is water enough to stay hydrated?
reply: A sports drink is water with sugar and salt, and it only earns its place in a long or hot session: over about an hour, or two sessions in a day, or a match in the heat. For an ordinary gym hour, a 5k or a swim, water is enough - a 500ml bottle of sports drink is about 30g of sugar, and the salt you lose is replaced by the next meal.

instruction: I'm a new basketball coach and I'm looking for some advice on how to motivate my players.
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm planning a trip and I'm thinking of taking an overnight train. What's the main advantage of overnight trains?
reply: Coaches are the cheapest way between two cities: booked two or three weeks ahead a long trip is often under 20 pounds when the train is over 60, and the overnight coach saves a hotel night as well. Book on the operator's own site or app, take the ticket on your phone, and put the big bag in the hold, which is included but has to be tagged.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my daily commute to work easier. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming art festivals in my area. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm planning to make a salad for dinner. What's in season right now?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm trying to improve my work performance. What are some key factors that affect the quality of work?
reply: Two sentences: your job title and what you actually do in a week, then one thing you have changed or finished. "I am a warehouse team leader - I run a shift of eight, and I have just moved us onto scanners, which cut picking errors." Thirty seconds is plenty; they are testing whether you can be brief and whether the last job taught you anything.

instruction: I'm curious about colors. How do we see colors?
reply: The Sun sends out every colour mixed together, so from space it looks white; through our air the blue is scattered away and what reaches you looks yellow-white. Low in the sky it looks orange because the light crosses even more air on the way in.

instruction: I'm having trouble with traffic in my city. What are some common traffic management systems?
reply: Join on the slip road at the speed of the traffic already there, because arriving slowly is the thing that makes it frightening: mirror, indicate, then match the lorries in the left lane. Keep left unless you are overtaking, leave a two-second gap to the car in front (double it in rain, and further in spray at night), and do not sit alongside a lorry where the driver cannot see you.

instruction: I like playing sports and exercising. What's the most important thing in sports?
reply: Ten minutes is plenty: a jog to get warm, then leg swings, side-steps, lunges and a few short sprints, and finish with the ball or the equipment so the last thing you do looks like the game. Save the long stretches for afterwards.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, do you have any suggestions for electronic music?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm planning to cook for my family this weekend, do you have any kid-friendly recipe ideas?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I don't know what to wear. Can you help me?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I want to make a pie, but I don't know where to start. What ingredients do I need for a basic apple pie?
reply: Start with something they can eat: cut an apple into four, take one piece - that is one quarter. Then show that the bottom number is how many pieces the whole was cut into and the top is how many you have.

instruction: I'm a new parent and I'm worried about my home's safety for my baby. What are some basic things I can do to child-proof my home?
reply: Decide in advance what you will do and how long you will stay, and tell people early so nobody is surprised on the day. Have one safe topic and one exit ready ('we need to get the little one home'), and step outside for ten minutes when it heats up.

instruction: I'm going to a formal event and I'm looking for an evening gown. What are some popular colors for evening gowns?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I have two kids, a boy and a girl. What are some fun activities to do with them?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm interested in photography. What are some basic techniques I should know?
reply: Get closer and hold the phone still: brace it against a wall, a table or your chest, and tap the screen on the person or thing you are shooting so the brightness is set for that and not for the sky behind. Wipe the lens on your sleeve first, because a smeared lens is what makes phone photos look flat and hazy.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the violin. When was it invented?
reply: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) was the German composer who carried classical music into the romantic age, from the Fifth Symphony to the Ninth and its Ode to Joy. He was going deaf from his late twenties and still wrote some of his greatest music once he could no longer hear it played.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are the main food groups?
reply: Carbohydrates are one of the main food groups: sugars and starches that the body breaks down into glucose for energy. Bread, rice, pasta, potatoes, fruit and sugar are carbohydrates, and fibre is a carbohydrate the body cannot digest.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Thai cuisine. What's a popular Thai dish?
reply: Order the thing you would not cook at home, and get one more dish than there are people so there is something left cold for tomorrow: a shared starter, a main each, one side for two people. On a Chinese that is a soup or the salt and pepper ribs, two mains with rice between them, and a vegetable; on an Indian it is a dry dish and a wet one, a bread and a rice, not three curries; on a chippy it is one large chips for two.

instruction: I'm getting married soon and I'm trying to decide on a wedding theme. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: It's really hot outside. What should I wear?
reply: Loose, light cotton in a pale colour is the coolest thing to wear, because it lets air through and reflects the sun; a wide hat and sunglasses are worth more than another layer of sunscreen. Keep shoulders covered over a long day and wear shoes you can walk in on hot tarmac.

instruction: I'm worried about the storm that's coming to my area. What's the latest forecast?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do you know anything about dreams?
reply: Nightmares usually follow stress, late food, alcohol or a heavy film before bed, so start there. If the same one keeps coming back, write it down in the day and rehearse a different ending a few times: that is the technique that works.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding social media etiquette. What's the rule about following someone back on social media?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account. Private means new people have to ask to follow you, but it does not hide anything from the people already following, so check that list too.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried about her health. When should I take her to the vet for a check-up?
reply: From about eight, twice a year is worth it: the vet can find the things old cats hide — kidney trouble, thyroid, arthritis, high blood pressure — before you see them. Weigh her monthly at home and ask for a blood and urine test at the annual visit.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the nervous system does.
reply: The brain is a network of about 86 billion nerve cells that talk to each other through electrical and chemical signals. Different regions handle different jobs - movement, sight, language, emotion and memory - and the connections between them are what let you think, learn and remember; it runs on about 20 percent of the body's energy.

instruction: I'm looking for professional cleaning services for my home. What's the typical cost for a one-time deep cleaning?
reply: A cleaner is usually £12 to £18 an hour, so a two-hour weekly visit is £25 to £40, and a one-off deep clean of a three-bedroom house is £60 to £120. An agency costs more than someone working for themselves but covers insurance, tax and holidays.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my pantry. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: A pantry or larder is a cool, dark, dry cupboard for the food that keeps: tins, dried pasta and rice, flour, sugar, oil, spices. Cool and dry matter more than size - a shelf by a radiator or a sunny window turns flour and rice stale and brings weevils - so put it on an outside wall away from the cooker.

instruction: What are negative numbers?
reply: An integer is a whole number - positive, negative or zero - with no fraction or decimal part. So 4, -7 and 0 are integers, while 2.5 and 1/3 are not; the integers are the counting numbers, their negatives, and zero.

instruction: I'm interested in the Winter Olympics. What sports are included?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: What are some popular soft drinks?
reply: Gin wants tonic about one to three with a big wedge of lemon or lime, and cucumber or a sprig of rosemary if you have it; vodka takes the same plus elderflower or ginger beer, dark rum wants ginger beer and a squeeze of lime, whisky wants soda or ginger ale, and tequila wants grapefruit soda and salt. Cheap tonic is fine but use plenty of ice and stir it, because a warm, flat G and T tastes of nothing.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to work out at home. What's a good piece of equipment to start with?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm planning to walk my dog later and I was wondering how long I should walk him for.
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I only want to work during the summer months. Do you know of any seasonal jobs?
reply: Take the train or the coach between cities instead of flying, book a month or two ahead, and stay in hostels or travel out of season: May, June and late September cost about half what August does. Eat where people work - market stalls, bakeries, a supermarket lunch - and choose one small town over a second capital.

instruction: I'm a high school senior and I'm excited about graduation. What's a popular tradition for graduates?
reply: Buy to the list the school sends, not to the supermarket display, and buy two of the things that get worn out: two jumpers with the badge, two or three polo shirts, two pairs of trousers or skirts, a PE kit in the school colours and plimsolls for indoors. A child starting in reception also needs a spare set of clothes in a bag for the first weeks and wellies if they play outside.

instruction: I'm trying to decide whether to live in a city or a rural area. What are some differences between the two?
reply: Book direct with a small hotel or guesthouse once you know roughly where you want to be: a phone call often beats the price on the booking site, and it is the cheapest way in small towns. Hostels and apart-hotels win for a week, and a kitchen saves more than a lower nightly rate.

instruction: I'm on my lunch break at work and I was wondering if you had any suggestions for things to do during my free time.
reply: Leave at nap time or early if you can, plan a stop or a walk about every two hours, and pack snacks, water, sunshades and a tablet with films downloaded. A surprise bag of small new things to hand out one at a time is the trick for the last hour.

instruction: I'm thinking of making some fried chicken for dinner, but I've never deep-fried anything before. What do I need to get started?
reply: Three things keep a fried coating crisp: a dry surface, oil that is hot enough, and air under it once it is out. Pat the food dry and flour it before the egg and crumbs, because a wet surface steams from the inside; fry at about 175C to 180C, which is a cube of bread browning in 60 seconds, since cooler oil soaks in and hotter oil browns the outside before the middle is done.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new teaching methods. What do you think about project-based learning?
reply: Help them shrink it to one question they can answer on a page - not the whole subject, but one thing about it - then one page of notes from one book or site, in their own words. A project is marked on the child's reading and thinking, so doing it for them shows in the writing and they learn nothing: sit beside them, ask what they already know, and hand back the pen.

instruction: I'm looking for information about luxury fashion brands. What are some popular ones?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm a collector of old coins and I'm interested in learning more about authenticating them. Where should I start?
reply: Start with Companies House, which is free: search the name or the number on their quote and you can see whether the company exists, when it was formed and whether the registered address is a real place rather than a mail drop - a limited company has to put its number and registered address on its website and its invoices. Then the trade checks: a written quote rather than a verbal one, proof of insurance, and for gas, oil or electrical work the registration number you can check yourself on the Gas Safe, OFTEC or NICEIC register.

instruction: I'm looking for new sunglasses. What are some popular styles?
reply: Loose, light cotton in a pale colour is the coolest thing to wear, because it lets air through and reflects the sun; a wide hat and sunglasses are worth more than another layer of sunscreen. Keep shoulders covered over a long day and wear shoes you can walk in on hot tarmac.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to save money on my daily commute to work. I've heard of carpooling apps, but I don't know much about them.
reply: Anything wholly and necessarily for the work: stock and materials, tools, software and subscriptions, insurance, bank fees, the business share of your phone and broadband, travel between jobs (not the commute), and a share of the heating if you work at home. Keep the receipt and note what it was for.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some healthy cooking methods?
reply: Butter first, then something sharp or salty on top: peanut butter and sliced banana, mashed avocado with salt and lemon, beans with a dash of Worcestershire, or a tin of sardines on hot toast. Cheese on toast under the grill for 3 minutes is the fastest good one, and a sliced tomato under the cheese stops it going dry.
