instruction: I'm looking for some new shoes, but I don't want to go to the mall. Can I do some digital window shopping instead?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I have a big family with lots of siblings. What is a sibling?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I'm having trouble with order of operations in math. What does PEMDAS stand for?
reply: Algebra is arithmetic with letters standing in for numbers, so a rule works for every number at once: if a notebook costs n pounds, three cost 3n. The letters are called variables, and the usual job is to rearrange an equation until the letter is alone.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow, and I was wondering what I should do to prepare.
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of pies?
reply: Bake something that is low in sugar by nature rather than swapping in sweeteners: an almond and olive oil cake, a carrot cake made with less sugar and more spice, or berries with cream and a little dark chocolate. Keep the portion small and have it after a meal rather than on its own, and put the fruit and the cream on the plate so the cake slice can be thinner.

instruction: I'm interested in trail running. What are some key things I should know before I start?
reply: Nothing new on the day: the shoes, socks and kit you did your long runs in, plus your race number, safety pins, a bottle, and the gels or sweets you have practised with. Eat the breakfast you have tested, get there an hour early, and set off slower than feels right.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping because of my shift work schedule. Do you have any tips?
reply: Pick one stretch of daytime to sleep and guard it like a night: straight home, dark room, phone off, and the same hours seven days a week, including days off, so your body clock settles. Wear sunglasses on the way home and keep the bedroom cold, and take a short nap before the shift rather than a long one after it.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what's the difference between a mixture and a solution.
reply: A solution is a mixture where one substance dissolves in another: the dissolved substance is the solute and the liquid it goes into is the solvent. Salt water and sugar water are solutions, and the dissolved part cannot be filtered out.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with the marketing team. Do you have any tips?
reply: Aim for two real conversations rather than working the room: ask what they are working on and what brought them there, then listen. Have one sentence ready about yourself and follow up with a two-line message the next day.

instruction: I'm looking for casual wear ideas, but I'm not sure what styles suit my body type. I have an hourglass figure.
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm a high school student and I'm interested in computer science. What is computer science?
reply: ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who is the all-time leading scorer in the NBA?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm feeling overwhelmed with work and struggling to disconnect after hours. Do you have any tips for achieving a better work-life balance?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm looking for a good pair of running shoes. What should I look for?
reply: For running, yes: a proper pair makes a real difference to your knees, and a running shop will watch you run and fit you for £90 to £130. Replace them every 500 to 800km, or when the midsole feels flat.

instruction: I'm flying to New York tomorrow and I'm not sure about the luggage restrictions.
reply: Start with the airline, because cabin sizes differ: a 55x40x20cm case fits most paid cabin allowances, while the free underseat bag is around 40x20x25cm, and a bag outside the airline's own limit is the one thing that gets charged at the gate. Four wheels and a hard polycarbonate shell survive the hold better, soft bags give and squash into a car; either way check the empty weight against a 23kg allowance and buy from a brand that covers wheels and handles for years rather than months.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet for my family, do you think it's a good idea?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: What are the different phases of the moon?
reply: The Moon doesn't change shape; half of it is always lit by the sun, and we see a different slice of that lit half as it orbits the Earth. A full moon takes about 29.5 days to come round again.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise routine and I'm interested in circuit training. What is circuit training?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm planning to go to the outlet mall this weekend. Do you have any tips for outlet shopping?
reply: Buy for the first night, not for the shelves: a takeaway voucher for the evening the boxes are still out, a box with loo roll, tea, milk, mugs, bin bags, a corkscrew and a phone charger, or a hot meal you turn up with. A plant, a good bottle or a decent set of tea towels all last longer than another candle, and a voucher for a hardware shop is the unromantic one people are pleased about.

instruction: I'm starting a vegetable garden. What are some easy vegetables to grow?
reply: Grow what gives you a lot from a little: salad leaves, radishes, spring onions, dwarf beans, cherry tomatoes, chillies, one courgette plant, herbs in a pot by the door, and strawberries in a basket. Go upwards where you can - beans and cucumbers up a frame, tomatoes in a grow bag - and sow a few seeds every three weeks rather than everything at once, so you eat from June to October instead of facing a glut in August.

instruction: I'm trying to study more effectively. What's active recall?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's a popular genre right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my wardrobe. What are the current street style trends?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I've been noticing a lot of noise pollution in my neighborhood lately. What is noise pollution?
reply: If the noise is coming from outside your room, earplugs and a heavy curtain take the edge off, and a fan or white noise can mask it. If it is a neighbour and it happens often, your council's noise team can act on it; a short log of the times is what they ask for.

instruction: I'm looking for a new set of kitchen utensils. What are the must-haves for a beginner?
reply: One 20cm cook's knife does almost everything, so spend the money there - around 25 to 40 pounds on a forged one with a full tang gets an edge that holds - and add a serrated bread knife and a small paring knife when you need them, rather than buying a set of six cheap ones that none of them do a job well. Hold it before you buy it, because the handle has to fill your hand, and only buy something you can sharpen yourself with a steel or a stone.

instruction: I have a dull knife in my kitchen. What can I do to sharpen it?
reply: Ten strokes a side on a steel brings a blunt edge back for a week; a whetstone, coarse side then fine, once a month is what actually sharpens it. Hold the blade at 20 degrees, keep the fingers of your other hand behind the edge, and wash and dry it by hand: a dishwasher blunts a knife and splits a wooden handle.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting techniques?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm looking for a way to cook my food faster. What is pressure cooking?
reply: Butter first, then something sharp or salty on top: peanut butter and sliced banana, mashed avocado with salt and lemon, beans with a dash of Worcestershire, or a tin of sardines on hot toast. Cheese on toast under the grill for 3 minutes is the fastest good one, and a sliced tomato under the cheese stops it going dry.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What are some popular competitive cooking shows?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm looking for a new bike helmet. What should I consider when choosing one?
reply: Wear one: it is not the law for adults in the UK, but a helmet is the difference between a bruise and a head injury in the one fall nobody plans for. It does not make you safe from traffic, so ride as if it were not there: take the lane at junctions and never go up the left side of a lorry.

instruction: I'm going to Paris soon and I want to bring back some souvenirs for my friends and family. What are some popular items to buy?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm having trouble meeting deadlines at work. What are some common factors that affect job performance?
reply: It means leaving almost no time to spare. What is the deadline?

instruction: I'm worried about winter coming, what can I do to prepare?
reply: Pack for 2 to 8C, wind and rain: a waterproof coat with a hood, warm layers you can take off indoors, and shoes you can walk a hill in. It gets dark around 4pm in December, so a small torch and plans for the afternoon indoors help.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What's the main difference between digital and film cameras?
reply: ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the solar system. What is the biggest planet?
reply: Jupiter is the biggest planet: about 143,000 km across, or 11 Earths side by side, and more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

instruction: I've been feeling tired lately and I want to know how I can improve my overall health.
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some popular pets for beginners?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I have a dog that gets really anxious during grooming. What can I do to make it easier for him?
reply: A growl while he is being brushed or handled is him saying it hurts or frightens him, so stop as soon as he does it and never tell him off for it - a dog punished for the warning goes straight to the snap. Run your hands over him first, because mats behind the ears, a tight collar and a sore ear or hip are the usual causes, and a dog who has always been fine and has just started wants a vet check.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family who live far away. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: A relative going quiet is usually nothing more than a busy year. Send something small and specific - a photo, or a plain 'I've missed you, are you around for a call?' - rather than a note about how long it has been.

instruction: I'm looking to improve my skills at work. What are some ways to do that?
reply: Make the task visible and small: one page, one timer, everything else out of the room. Body-doubling works for a lot of people - study alongside someone, in person or on a video call with mics off.

instruction: I'm looking for a new baseball bat. What types are available?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm looking for a new video game to play, but I'm not sure what type I want. What are some popular video game genres?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I'm not sure if my workplace allows them.
reply: Ask in writing before you get the animal, because a tenancy that says no pets is a term you can ask to have changed but not one you can ignore: put the animal in the letter - the kind, its age, that it is house-trained and insured - offer to have the carpets cleaned when you leave and to put right anything it damages, and ask for a written answer. A landlord can say no, but in England a blanket ban with no way to ask is the kind of term consumer law lets you challenge, so a reasoned refusal in writing is worth having before you take it further.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Can Feng shui help me?
reply: Stand up and move for two minutes every half hour, drink water, and put a bright light on your face — sleepiness at a desk is often boredom plus warm air. Do the hardest thing first and leave the reading for when you are flagging.

instruction: I'm planning a weekend trip to the beach. What are some popular beach activities?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed about my parents. They're always on my case about something.
reply: Treat it as information before it is a battle: something at school is usually behind it - a friendship, a lesson, a child or a teacher - so ask the teacher for the pattern of the days they refuse. Keep the morning calm and small (clothes out the night before, one step at a time), get them through the gate even for a short day, and ask the GP about anxiety if it goes on for more than a fortnight.

instruction: I'm trying to manage my budget and I'm having trouble deciding what I should spend my money on. Can you help me figure out what I need versus what I want?
reply: Write down what comes in each month, then what goes out in two piles: the fixed ones (rent, bills, travel, debt) and the ones you decide week by week (food, going out, clothes). What is left is what you can save or throw at a debt, and if the piles add up to more than comes in, cut from the weekly ones first because that is where the slack is.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Do you know any good sleep apps?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: What is a mountain?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I've been working out for months, but I feel like I've hit a plateau. I'm not seeing any progress or improvement in my fitness level.
reply: Three half-hour sessions a week is enough to feel different in a month, and you need no equipment: a walk or a jog for ten minutes to warm up, then squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a hip hinge, and a plank, two rounds of each. Push into the last two or three of every set and add a rep each week, because that progression is what changes anything.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about classical music. What are some popular classical music genres?
reply: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) was the German composer who carried classical music into the romantic age, from the Fifth Symphony to the Ninth and its Ode to Joy. He was going deaf from his late twenties and still wrote some of his greatest music once he could no longer hear it played.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about ancient civilizations. Can you tell me about the pyramids in Egypt?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Disneyland. Are there any hotels within the park?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about music festivals. What's the biggest music festival in the world?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for live music venues in my area. Can you tell me some popular ones?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: What is magnetism?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm worried about staying healthy. What are some basic things I can do to stay healthy while traveling?
reply: Eat where it is busy and freshly cooked, and have it hot: a queue and a hotplate are better signs than a clean table. Have bottled or filtered water and the ice made from it, peel your own fruit, and skip the raw salad that a kitchen has washed in tap water.

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. What's the name of our local minor league baseball team?
reply: Split the pitch into four small squares and put three or four children in each with one ball: everyone touches the ball, nobody can chase the whole crowd. Rotate the squares every five minutes so they meet each other, and finish with a game on a short, wide pitch so there is always someone to pass to.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in nature. What shapes do we see in flowers?
reply: In the flower: pollen from the male part (the stamen) lands on the sticky tip (the stigma), and a tube grows down to the ovule at the base. The fertilised ovule becomes the seed and the ovary around it swells into the fruit - which is why every fruit has seeds inside.

instruction: I'm going shopping for some groceries and I want to compare prices. What's the best way to do that?
reply: If the bill charges more than the shelf price or the menu, ask for the difference back: the price displayed is the price you pay. If they refuse, keep the receipt and a photo of the label or the menu, complain in writing, then use a chargeback or the small claims court.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a bike for commuting to work. What safety gear do I need?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm looking for free online educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What's the main cause?
reply: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere instead of letting it escape to space. That extra heat raises average temperatures, melts ice and makes extreme weather more likely; the science is settled, though predicting any one storm is not.

instruction: I want to get fit, but I'm having trouble staying motivated. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about renewable energy sources.
reply: Nearly all of it is made by spinning a generator: gas, coal, nuclear, wind and water all turn the same kind of shaft, and the National Grid carries the result around the country and steps the voltage down through substations to your street. Solar panels are the odd ones out - they make it straight from light, with nothing turning.

instruction: My internet is slow. What affects internet speed?
reply: Test the speed on a cable or right next to the router first, because that tells you whether the problem is the broadband or the wifi. If it is the wifi, move closer, use 5GHz, and check how many devices are streaming; if the cabled speed is also low, it is your provider and worth a call.

instruction: I'm looking for information about bus rapid transit. What is it?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm going to work and I'm worried about traffic. Is rush hour over?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my garage. Do you have any tips?
reply: One room at a time, three bags on the floor — bin, donate, keep — and the donate bags go to the car the same day or they drift back. Ten minutes a day beats a lost weekend, and start with the room you walk through most, because clearing that one is what makes the rest of the house feel possible.

instruction: I want to make a simple vegetarian dish for dinner. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Make the vegetarian dish the main for the whole table and put the meat on the side as an extra: a mushroom and lentil lasagne, a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. Nobody gets a plate of sides, and you cook one dinner.

instruction: I'm interested in fashion trends. What's popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape for soccer season. What's a good way to start training?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape for soccer season. What's a good exercise for building endurance?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm planning to buy a new laptop online, but I'm not sure which website to choose from since the prices seem to vary.
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for a new car and want to know which fuel type is most efficient.
reply: The four that give the most back: tyres at the right pressure, nothing heavy in the boot, gentle acceleration and a steady 50 to 60mph instead of 70-plus on the motorway. Air con costs you fuel at low speed, so use the window around town and the air con on the motorway.

instruction: I'm going to Japan for my sister's birthday and I want to get her a gift. What are some gift-giving customs I should know about in Japan?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I want to make a budget for my shopping, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Start from the money you need, not from what feels cheeky: add up your yearly costs (tools, insurance, software, travel, a phone) and the income you want to take home, add about a third on top for tax and quiet weeks, then divide by the days you can actually bill - about 220 a year if you work full time, and far fewer if you spend half the week on admin and chasing work. That gives a day rate; an hourly rate is that divided by six or seven.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular types of crafts?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I want to eat healthier, but I'm not sure where to start. What's the most important thing to focus on?
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer.

instruction: I'm having trouble with multiplication. Can you explain what it means to multiply two numbers?
reply: In maths a power tells you how many times to multiply a number by itself: 3 to the power 4 means 3 x 3 x 3 x 3, which is 81. The small raised number is the exponent and the number being multiplied is the base; a square is a power of 2 and a cube is a power of 3.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the mall this weekend. What can I expect to find there?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do dreams affect our mental health?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in street photography. What are some good cities to visit for street photography?
reply: Tokyo has about 14 million people in the city, and about 37 million in the wider metro area, which makes it the biggest in the world.

instruction: I'm interested in sports. What's the oldest sport in the world?
reply: The Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, worked out from meteorites and the oldest rocks. Life got going within the first billion years, and everything humans have done fits into the last tiny sliver of that time.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. How many hours of sleep do I need each night?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas on what to have for breakfast with my family. We're getting bored with the same old routine.
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm looking for a new suit, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm trying to get more vitamins in my diet, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: Is it going to be sunny today?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a new smartphone. What's the main difference between a good camera phone and a regular one?
reply: Three things settle it, and none of them is the model year. If what you have still holds a charge to the evening, opens apps without a wait and still gets security updates, a new phone buys you a better camera and a nicer screen rather than a faster life, so waiting a year costs you nothing.

instruction: I'm really interested in gardening. What are some common things people harvest from their gardens?
reply: Insects and worms from lawns and dung, then fruit, seeds and scraps; in autumn they switch to berries and orchards, which is when the murmurations gather before roosting. A starling will also take fat balls and kitchen scraps from a feeder.

instruction: I just bought some chicken breasts and I'm not sure how to store them properly.
reply: Dissolve about 50g of salt in a litre of cold water - roughly 2 litres for a whole bird - and keep it in the fridge for an hour for every kg, or overnight for a chicken. A big pan or a clean bag works, with something on top to keep the bird under.

instruction: I'm going to my first concert next week and I'm not sure what to expect. What's the etiquette for arriving at a concert venue?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm thinking about food. What are some common meals people eat for breakfast?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm looking for a new ingredient to try in my cooking. What's a popular international ingredient?
reply: Ras el hanout is a Moroccan blend and not usually hot - cumin, coriander, cinnamon, ginger and pepper - though some jars have chilli in. A tablespoon for a tagine or a tray of vegetables.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about a traditional holiday in Japan?
reply: Late March to early April, moving north as the season goes: Tokyo usually peaks around the end of March, Kyoto a few days later. Book accommodation months ahead, and be flexible, because a cold spring can delay it by a week or two.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas for a day trip near my city. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with my friends. What types of board games are there?
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook.

instruction: I'm going to use a taxi tonight and I'm a bit worried about safety. What are some general safety tips for taking a taxi?
reply: Get left and off the carriageway if you still can, then hazards on. Everyone out of the doors on the left, behind the barrier, and well back from the car: never stand between it and the traffic, and never change a wheel on a motorway.

instruction: I'm feeling really stressed at work. Do you have any strategies for maintaining a good work-life balance?
reply: Look at the week before the people: what is due, who is covering it, and what can be moved or dropped, then take one real thing off the list this week and say out loud why you moved it - a team that is flat is usually carrying more than its hours, and a speech about wellbeing does not buy that back. Then ten minutes with each of them, one at a time, and ask which part of the week is heaviest rather than whether they are coping: the one task they dread is the one you can shift, and it is rarely the one you guess.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my dog. He's been barking a lot lately and I don't know why.
reply: Practise the whole thing rather than the bark: put him on a lead, have someone ring the bell or knock, and ask for a sit a few steps back from the door before it opens. Reward the sit, not the silence.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new puppy and I'm wondering how I can help it get along with my other pets.
reply: Meet on neutral ground, one walker each, and walk them side by side rather than face to face, then let them off lead only in a fenced space where the older dog can walk away. At home give the older dog his own bed, bowl and corner that the puppy cannot reach, feed them apart, and step in before the puppy hangs off his ears.

instruction: I'm learning about community helpers. What are some examples?
reply: Start with a free needs assessment from the council - it opens the door to home help, grab rails and a care package without you paying privately first. Then take the falls out of the house: rugs taped down, a light by the bed, a shower seat, a keysafe so help can get in.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need some help with my shopping list. Do you have any seasonal shopping lists available?
reply: Fix a total you can pay for in cash this month, divide it by the people you buy for, and write the cap next to each name before you open a browser. Buy in October, agree a secret santa with the adults, and shop for food from a list in early December: the overspend is nearly always late presents and a trolley filled in a panic.

instruction: I was wondering what magnets are used for.
reply: A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field, which pulls on iron, nickel and cobalt and pushes or pulls on other magnets. In most fridge magnets the field comes from tiny magnetic regions lined up in the same direction; in a compass needle it comes from a small piece of magnetised metal.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get involved in my community. What are some common volunteer opportunities?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding some of my school reading assignments. Do you have any strategies that might help?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm looking for some new casual shoes. What's popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for a new chew toy for my dog. What types of materials are safe for dogs to chew on?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I want to save money. Do you have any tips?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm putting together a basic first aid kit. What are some essential items I should include?
reply: A home kit is a box you can use one-handed in the dark: plasters in a few sizes, sterile gauze and tape, a crepe bandage, small scissors, tweezers, disposable gloves, a thermometer, and children's paracetamol with the dose worked out by weight. Add an ice pack, antiseptic cream and the 111 number, then check it once a year and replace anything past its date.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about high-speed rail. What is it?
reply: It means quick and on top of things. What is it they are on top of?

instruction: I'm interested in gardening as a hobby. What are some types of gardens I can have?
reply: *Gardeners' Question Time* is the one to start with: three experts answering listeners' questions, so you get the answer to the thing you were wondering about. *Talking Gardens* is the interview version and *The RHS Podcast* the seasonal jobs.

instruction: My family and I just moved into a new home, and we're planning a housewarming party. What are some common things people do to celebrate a new home?
reply: Bring the things that make the room theirs and give you something to do together: a framed photo, a small photo album, their own blanket or cardigan, a radio or a favourite mug, and a newspaper or a box of their usual sweets. Check what the room already has and what the home allows before you buy anything, and take one thing a visit rather than a car load - it is the visits, not the stuff, that make the room theirs.

instruction: I'm looking for information about film festivals. Are there any big ones happening soon?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for a simple meal prep idea for this week. What's a good place to start?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm looking for a new tea to try. What are some popular tea varieties?
reply: Nearly all of it is the same leaf at different levels of oxidation: green tea is dried before it can darken and tastes grassy, black tea is fully oxidised and malty, and oolong sits between them, roasted and floral. White tea is the young leaf barely processed, light and sweet, and pu-erh is aged and earthy, an acquired taste.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, do you have any suggestions for country music?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm looking for a new refrigerator. What are some popular brands?
reply: Stand a fridge thermometer in a glass of water on the middle shelf and leave it overnight: the fridge wants 3 to 5C and the freezer -18C, and the dial's numbers are not degrees. A fridge that will not reach it wants the door seals checked - close the door on a sheet of paper and see if it slides out easily - and the coils at the back dusted.

instruction: I like playing basketball and watching sports. Who is your favorite basketball player?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. What are night terrors?
reply: Take the fear seriously without feeding it: check the room together with the light on, leave a small lamp or the door ajar, and give a boring, calm bedtime routine at the same time each night. Nightmares are normal at four to six and usually ease; if a child is terrified most nights for weeks, mention it to the health visitor or GP.

instruction: I'm trying to find my signature style. What's a good way to start?
reply: The free way: open it in Adobe Acrobat Reader and use Fill & Sign, draw or type your signature once, then drag it onto the line and save a copy. On a Mac, Preview has Markup > Sign; on a phone, the Files app on an iPhone and Google Drive's annotate tool both do it.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable shoes. Do you know anything about orthopedic shoes?
reply: Support under the arch matters more than cushioning: a shoe with a firm heel counter and a removable insole you can swap for an arch-support one (about £20 to £40 from a pharmacy) is enough for most people with flat feet. A lace-up trainer with a straight shape and a snug midfoot holds the foot better than a slip-on, and if your feet, shins or knees hurt when you walk, or one arch has dropped recently, a podiatrist is worth the visit.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school. What is the fastest bone in the human body?
reply: An adult has 206 bones; a baby is born with roughly 270, and many of those fuse together as you grow. The smallest are three tiny ones in each middle ear.

instruction: I'm looking for sports that are good for people with disabilities. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm looking for information about factory work environments. What is a typical factory work environment like?
reply: *How I Built This* has the founder of one company telling how it actually started, in an hour, and it is the most useful one if you are thinking of starting something. *The Bottom Line* puts three bosses in a room and asks them the same question, and *StartUp* follows one company from the first day, mistakes included.

instruction: I'm learning about ecosystems in school. What is a food web?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. How many hours of sleep should I be getting?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: I'm planning a game night with friends and I need some suggestions for board games.
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I want to make sure I don't forget anything. What's the best way to make a grocery list?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for yoga classes near my home. Do you know any good studios?
reply: Go at the time you would actually go, on a weekday evening if that is when you are free: a gym that is full at six is the one you stop using. Then check three things - the distance from home or work, because anything past fifteen minutes gets skipped, whether the classes you want are included in the price or cost extra, and the notice period on the contract, which is often a month and sometimes three.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some nutritious foods I should include in my meals?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics and family trees. What is heredity?
reply: DNA is the long molecule that carries the instructions for building and running a living thing, written in a four-letter code. Genes are sections of it, and they are copied from parents to offspring.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. What are some popular walking tours?
reply: Plan for half the walking and twice the sitting: one or two things a day with a cafe or a bench between them, and a taxi or the hop-on bus for the long hops rather than marching between sights. Check step-free access before you book, because most museums, galleries and cathedrals publish it, ask the hotel for a room near the lift, and book help ahead on trains and at the airport - it is free, UK rail's Passenger Assist takes bookings up to 24 hours ahead and airports usually want 48.

instruction: I'm looking for some new toys for my dog. What are some popular pet toys?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I want to bake a cake, but I don't know what makes it rise.
reply: A cake rises on three things - the air you beat in, the bubbles the raising agent makes, and steam - and when it does not, the culprit is nearly always baking powder past its date (a teaspoon per 150g of plain flour, or use self-raising), the flour beaten in too hard once it went in, or the oven door opened in the first 20 minutes. Cream the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, fold the flour in with a spoon, fill the tin two-thirds full, and bake at 180C (160C fan) without opening the door.

instruction: I'm interested in mountain biking. What kind of bike do I need?
reply: A hybrid or gravel bike with 32 to 40mm tyres, mudguard and rack mounts and disc brakes: those stop in the wet and take a pannier. £500 to £800 new, £200 to £350 secondhand.

instruction: I'm flying to New York tomorrow. What kind of in-flight meals do they usually serve?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school. What's the difference between a balanced and an unbalanced force?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: What should I do if someone gets heatstroke?
reply: Hold the knob in for twenty seconds after the flame catches, then let it go: a pilot that won't hold is nearly always the thermocouple, a small part a Gas Safe engineer swaps in ten minutes. A draught or a dirty jet does it too, and both mean taking the case off, so that is their job as well.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my office more comfortable. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I'm heading to work and I want to know about traffic conditions.
reply: The national limits for cars are 30mph where there are street lights (unless signed otherwise), 60mph on a single carriageway and 70mph on a dual carriageway or motorway. They are a ceiling, not a target: on a narrow country lane 40mph is often too fast for the bends, and a lower sign overrides the national limit.

instruction: I'm interested in learning a musical instrument. What's a good instrument for a beginner?
reply: Say yes to a term of cheap lessons before you buy anything: school lessons or a group class cost a fraction of one-to-one, and four to six weeks tells you whether it will stick. Borrow or rent the instrument for that first term - a second-hand keyboard or guitar is thirty or forty pounds - and only buy once they have kept it up.

instruction: I'm looking for a new camera. What are some popular camera brands?
reply: Spend on the battery and the update years, not the camera: a mid-range phone at £250 to £400 lasts as long as a flagship if the maker promises four or five years of security updates (Samsung, Google and Apple do; many cheap brands promise two). Get at least 128GB, check the battery is 5,000mAh or more, and make sure it takes a physical SIM as well as an eSIM if you travel.

instruction: What is symmetry in shapes?
reply: Symmetry is when a shape or object looks the same after a fold, turn or flip. A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are mirror images - a square has four, a circle has infinitely many - and rotational symmetry is how many times it matches in a full turn.

instruction: I'm looking for a luxury travel experience. What's a popular destination for that?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: What was the first web browser?
reply: A browser is the program you read websites in: Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox are the common four and they all do the same job. Anything you type in the address bar, any page you save a password for and any tab you leave open belongs to that one browser, which is why an account that works on your phone can look lost on a laptop until you sign in.

instruction: I've been feeling really stressed out lately with work and I'm worried it's affecting my mental health. Do you have any tips for managing stress?
reply: Treat it as a work problem with a health cost, and act on both: tell your GP how it is affecting sleep, eating and mood, because a sick note and a few weeks off are normal and protect your job. At work, ask for the specific change that would help - fewer shifts, a different manager, a written plan - since adjustments are easier to say yes to than "less stress".

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What kind of paint should I use for a beginner?
reply: Heat and moving air are what dry a paint too fast, so keep the room cool and out of direct sun, shut the window and turn any fan off. Lid the tin and decant only what you will use in ten minutes, because a wide tray is all surface; a smaller tub keeps it workable.

instruction: I'm interested in music production. What software do you recommend for a beginner?
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: What color do you get when you mix red and blue?
reply: Blue is scattered much more strongly than green, so the green that is scattered arrives mixed with far more blue and the sky reads as pale blue. Violet is scattered even more, but there is less of it in sunlight and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so it never dominates.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some key things to include in a balanced diet?
reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm thinking of replacing my windows. What are the benefits of new windows?
reply: Widening a window opening is a builder's job, not a window fitter's: taking out brickwork under a new lintel is structural, where a swap of the same size is a fitter's morning. Ask a builder to price it, and a structural engineer if the wall carries the floor above; in a flat or a conservation area you may need permission too.

instruction: I'm looking for a new frying pan. What are some good materials?
reply: Olive oil or rapeseed oil is a good everyday choice: both are high in unsaturated fat and fine for normal frying. Save the extra virgin olive oil for salads and low heat, and use a plain vegetable oil when you need a very hot pan.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I don't know where to start. What's a good low-fat cooking method?
reply: You can eat well without cooking if you build the plate from the shop: a bag of salad or a punnet of tomatoes, ready-cooked chicken or a tin of tuna or chickpeas, and bread, couscous or a microwave pouch of rice. Frozen veg straight from the microwave is the cheapest half-plate of vegetables there is, and a pot of yogurt with fruit is pudding.

instruction: I'm having trouble talking to my family about my feelings. Do you have any advice?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I was thinking of starting a walk-to-work initiative in my neighborhood. Do you think it's a good idea?
reply: Parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday at 9am in a local park: register once online, print or screenshot your barcode, and turn up ten minutes early for the first-timers' briefing. Walkers are genuinely welcome and plenty of people walk it, so you will not be last on your own.

instruction: What is the most widely celebrated holiday in the world?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening, but I don't have a big outdoor space. Can I still garden?
reply: Garden leave is being paid to stay away from work during your notice period: you are still employed, still on the payroll and still bound by your contract, but told not to come in or to contact clients. You keep your holiday, your notice carries on running, and you are usually not allowed to start another job until it ends, so read the contract or ask HR before you take a new role.

instruction: I'm looking for some new YouTube channels to watch. What's popular right now?
reply: *Happy Valley* for tense British crime, *The Bear* for short, intense episodes, or *Detectorists* if you want something gentle and funny. All three are easy to watch with a partner.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What should I look for when reading food labels?
reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm thinking of setting up a home gym. What equipment do I need to get started?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I'm learning about endangered species. What is biodiversity?
reply: In biology, a niche is the job a species does where it lives: what it eats, when it is active, where it shelters and what eats it. Two species with the same niche in one place compete, and one usually wins or moves away.

instruction: I'm planning to make a video call with my family tonight. What features should I expect from a typical video call app?
reply: Treat it like a meeting, not a phone call: sit at a table with your notes, the job description and four stories written out in front of you - a week you organised, a difficult customer, something you fixed, a time you got it wrong and changed. Sit upright or stand, because the voice carries better.

instruction: I was wondering what magnets are made of.
reply: A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field, which pulls on iron, nickel and cobalt and pushes or pulls on other magnets. In most fridge magnets the field comes from tiny magnetic regions lined up in the same direction; in a compass needle it comes from a small piece of magnetised metal.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable technology. What are some popular types of wearable devices?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a wheel and axle?
reply: A gear is a toothed wheel that turns another wheel, so turning one turns the other at a different speed or with more force: a small gear driving a big one gives slow, strong, and the other way round gives fast, weak, which is how a bike's gears work.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to buy some souvenirs. What are some popular things to get?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Chinese cuisine. What's a popular Chinese dish?
reply: Fish and chips feeds a group for the least money and nobody argues about it. If tastes differ, Indian beats Chinese: more vegetarian mains, and the sides stretch, so two mains with one rice and one bread feeds three.

instruction: I'm planning to bake a cake, but I'm not sure if I should use milk or a milk alternative.
reply: Cold milk in a jar with a lid, shaken hard for 30 seconds and then 30 seconds in the microwave, gives a real foam with no machine, and a French press pumped up and down 15 times does the same. Whole milk froths best because the fat holds the bubbles, and stop heating at about 60 to 65C - past that the foam collapses and the milk tastes scalded.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sportswear brand to try. What's popular right now?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: What is a sofa?
reply: Measure the gap and the doorway before you argue, and take the legs or the door off if that is all that is stopping it: most sofas come apart at the back. Bought online or over the phone, you have 14 days to cancel and they have to collect a bulky item, though they can charge for that if the terms say so; bought in a shop, a return is their own policy, and something made to your measurements has no right to one.

instruction: I'm looking for some advice on what to wear during the transition from summer to fall.
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.

instruction: I'm concerned about storing chemicals in my home. What are some general tips?
reply: Anything with a hazard symbol on it is household chemicals, and the tip's hazardous waste skip is where it goes - most sites take it from householders, and a few councils run set days, so ring before you drive over. Keep it in its own labelled container, never mix two together, and never pour it down the drain or into the bin.

instruction: I'm learning about plate tectonics in school. What are the three main types of plate boundaries?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I'm looking for information about local sports leagues in my area. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What are climate models?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm interested in climate data collection. What are some common methods used to collect climate data?
reply: A biome is a large region with one climate and the plants and animals that go with it: rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, coral reef. The same biome turns up on different continents, because it is the climate that decides it.

instruction: I'm going to Paris soon and I want to buy some souvenirs. What are some popular things to buy there?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm looking for some behind-the-scenes content on my favorite TV show. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need to make a list. What's the best way to start?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm going to graduate soon and I was wondering, what's the point of alumni associations?
reply: College is further education: A-levels, BTECs, T-levels, apprenticeships and access courses, usually for 16 to 18 year olds and mostly free until 19. University is a degree, three or four years, with tuition loans and maintenance loans to pay for it.

instruction: It's a beautiful sunny day today, isn't it?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I have a parent-teacher conference coming up at my child's school. What should I expect?
reply: Believe them first and write down what happened, with dates and names, then ask the school for a meeting with the head of year rather than the class teacher alone. Ask what the school will do and when, and keep checking in with your child; if nothing changes in a few weeks, put it in writing and ask to see the head.

instruction: I'm interested in playing the piano, but I don't know where to find sheet music for beginners.
reply: Start with the treble clef only: the five lines are E, G, B, D, F from the bottom up and the four spaces spell FACE, and ten minutes a day of naming notes off a page is how it sticks. Then the same for the bass clef (Good Boys Do Fine Always on the lines), then note lengths and rests; a beginner tutor book and a free app like Tenuto cover it, and playing each note on the instrument as you name it is the part that makes it real.

instruction: I'm having some trouble understanding my family members sometimes, especially when we're not talking.
reply: A relative going quiet is usually nothing more than a busy year. Send something small and specific - a photo, or a plain 'I've missed you, are you around for a call?' - rather than a note about how long it has been.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about unusual musical instruments. Can you tell me about one?
reply: Start with the treble clef only: the five lines are E, G, B, D, F from the bottom up and the four spaces spell FACE, and ten minutes a day of naming notes off a page is how it sticks. Then the same for the bass clef (Good Boys Do Fine Always on the lines), then note lengths and rests; a beginner tutor book and a free app like Tenuto cover it, and playing each note on the instrument as you name it is the part that makes it real.
